records.name: QLS.Stoch.robbinsSiegmund_expBound
records.statement:
theorem robbinsSiegmund_expBound.{v}
    {Ω : Type v} [m0 : MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (ℱ : Filtration ℕ m0)
    (X Y Z W : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (adapted_X : Adapted ℱ X) (adapted_Y : Adapted ℱ Y)
    (adapted_Z : Adapted ℱ Z) (adapted_W : Adapted ℱ W)
    (predictable_Y : Adapted ℱ fun t => Y (t + 1))
    (predictable_Z : Adapted ℱ fun t => Z (t + 1))
    (predictable_W : Adapted ℱ fun t => W (t + 1))
    (hX_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ X t ω)
    (hY_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ Y t ω)
    (hZ_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ Z t ω)
    (hW_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ W t ω)
    (condexp_ineq : ∀ t,
      μ[fun ω => X (t + 1) ω | ℱ t]
        ≤ᵐ[μ] fun ω => (1 + Y (t + 1) ω) * X t ω + Z (t + 1) ω - W (t + 1) ω)
    (integrable_X : ∀ t, Integrable (X t) μ)
    (integrable_Z : ∀ t, Integrable (Z t) μ)
    (integrable_W : ∀ t, Integrable (W t) μ)
    (sumEZ : Summable (fun t => ∫ ω, Z t ω ∂μ))
    (prod_bound : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ t ω, prodY Y t ω ≤ C)
  : ∃ Xlim : Ω → ℝ,
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun t => X t ω) atTop (nhds (Xlim ω))) ∧
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Summable (fun t => W t ω)) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
Robbins–Siegmund variant under expectation-level summability and a uniform product bound.

Assumptions:
- Adaptedness/predictability for `X,Y,Z,W` as in the main theorem
- Nonnegativity: `0 ≤ X t ω, 0 ≤ Y t ω, 0 ≤ Z t ω, 0 ≤ W t ω`
- Integrability: `X t, Z t, W t` integrable for all `t`
- Drift: `μ[X_{t+1} | ℱ_t] ≤ (1+Y_{t+1}) X_t + Z_{t+1} - W_{t+1}` a.e.
- Expectation summability: `Summable (fun t => ∫ ω, Z t ω ∂μ)`
- Product bound: `∃ C > 0, ∀ t ω, prodY Y t ω ≤ C`

Conclusions:
- `X t` converges almost surely to a finite limit
- `∑ W t` is finite almost surely

signoffs.comment: S. Gadat, Lecture notes on Stochastic Optimization Algorithms, http://perso.math.univ-toulouse.fr/gadat/files/2012/12/cours_Algo_Stos_M2R5.pdf

records.name: QLS.Stoch.robbinsSiegmund_full
records.statement:
theorem robbinsSiegmund_full.{v}
    {Ω : Type v} [m0 : MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (ℱ : Filtration ℕ m0)
    (V U α β : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    -- Adaptedness
    (adapted_V : Adapted ℱ V)
    (adapted_α : Adapted ℱ α)
    (adapted_β : Adapted ℱ β)
    (adapted_U : Adapted ℱ U)
    -- Predictability (X_{n+1} is F_n-measurable)
    (predictable_α : Adapted ℱ fun t => α (t + 1))
    (predictable_β : Adapted ℱ fun t => β (t + 1))
    (predictable_U : Adapted ℱ fun t => U (t + 1))
    -- Nonnegativity
    (hV_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ V t ω)
    (hα_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ α t ω)
    (hβ_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ β t ω)
    (hU_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ U t ω)
    -- Integrability
    (integrable_V : ∀ t, Integrable (V t) μ)
    (integrable_β : ∀ t, Integrable (β t) μ)
    (integrable_U : ∀ t, Integrable (U t) μ)
    -- (ii) Product bound and β summability
    (prod_bound : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ t ω, prodY α t ω ≤ C)
    (sum_Eβ : Summable (fun t => ∫ ω, β t ω ∂μ))
    -- (iii) Drift inequality
    (condexp_ineq : ∀ t,
      μ[fun ω => V (t + 1) ω | ℱ t]
        ≤ᵐ[μ] fun ω => (1 + α (t + 1) ω) * V t ω + β (t + 1) ω - U (t + 1) ω)
  : -- Conclusions
    -- (a) V_n → V_∞ a.s. with V_∞ ∈ L¹, and sup E[V_n] < ∞
    (∃ Vlim : Ω → ℝ,
      Integrable Vlim μ ∧
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun t => V t ω) atTop (nhds (Vlim ω)))) ∧
    (BddAbove (Set.range fun n => ∫ ω, V n ω ∂μ)) ∧
    -- (b) ∑ U_n < ∞ a.s.
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Summable (fun t => U t ω)) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
Full Robbins-Siegmund theorem with L¹ limit and sup E[V] bound.

Assumptions:
- Adaptedness/predictability for `V, α, β, U`
- Nonnegativity: `0 ≤ V t ω, 0 ≤ α t ω, 0 ≤ β t ω, 0 ≤ U t ω`
- Integrability: `V t, β t, U t` integrable for all `t`
- Product bound: `∃ C > 0, ∀ t ω, prodY α t ω ≤ C`
- Summability: `Summable (fun t => ∫ ω, β t ω ∂μ)`
- Drift inequality: `μ[V_{t+1} | ℱ_t] ≤ (1+α_{t+1}) V_t + β_{t+1} - U_{t+1}` a.e.

Conclusions:
- `V_n → V_∞` a.s. with `V_∞ ∈ L¹`
- `sup E[V_n] < ∞`
- `∑ U_n < ∞` a.s.

signoffs.comment: S. Gadat, Lecture notes on Stochastic Optimization Algorithms, http://perso.math.univ-toulouse.fr/gadat/files/2012/12/cours_Algo_Stos_M2R5.pdf

records.name: convergence_stochastic_gradient_method
records.statement:
theorem convergence_stochastic_gradient_method
    (X : ℕ → Ω → E) (γ : ℕ → ℝ) (h : E → E) (ΔM R : ℕ → Ω → E) (V : E → ℝ) (gradV : E → E)
    (ℱ : Filtration ℕ m0)
    (proc : StochasticAlgorithm X γ h ΔM R)
    (asm : SGD_Convergence_Assumptions μ X γ h ΔM R V gradV ℱ) :
    -- (a) sup E[V(X_n)] < +∞
    (BddAbove (Set.range fun n => ∫ ω, V (X n ω) ∂μ)) ∧
    -- (b) ∑ γ_{n+1}⟨∇V, h⟩(X_n) < +∞ a.s.
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Summable (fun n => γ (n + 1) * @inner ℝ _ _ (gradV (X n ω)) (h (X n ω)))) ∧
    -- (c) V(X_n) → V_∞ ∈ L¹ a.s.
    (∃ V_inf : Ω → ℝ, Integrable V_inf μ ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => V (X n ω)) atTop (nhds (V_inf ω))) ∧
    -- (d) X_{n+1} - X_n → 0 a.s. and in L²
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => X (n + 1) ω - X n ω) atTop (nhds 0)) ∧
    (Tendsto (fun n => ∫ ω, ‖X (n + 1) ω - X n ω‖^2 ∂μ) atTop (nhds 0)) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
Theorem 2.3.6: Convergence of the Stochastic Gradient Method.

Under assumptions (H1) and (H2), one has:
(a) sup_{n≥0} E[V(X_n)] < +∞
(b) ∑_{n≥0} γ_{n+1}⟨∇V, h⟩(X_n) < +∞ a.s.
(c) V(X_n) → V_∞ ∈ L¹ a.s.
(d) X_n - X_{n-1} → 0 a.s. and in L²

records.name: SGDUniqueMin.convergence_simplified
records.statement:
theorem convergence_simplified
    (X : ℕ → Ω → E) (γ : ℕ → ℝ) (h : E → E) (ΔM : ℕ → Ω → E)
    (V : E → ℝ) (gradV : E → E) (ℱ : Filtration ℕ m0) (x_star : E)
    (asm : SimplifiedAssumptions μ X γ h ΔM V gradV ℱ x_star) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => X n ω) atTop (nhds x_star) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
Simplified Corollary 2.3.1: Almost sure convergence for unbiased SGD with bounded variance.

Under the simplified assumptions (unbiased gradients, constant variance bound), we have:
- X_n → x* almost surely

The proof is simpler because:
1. No remainder term R (so the earlier "line 1375" gap disappears)
2. Constant variance ⟹ E[‖∑ γ_k ΔM_k‖²] ≤ σ² ∑ γ_k² < ∞ directly
3. L²-bounded martingale converges a.s. by Doob's theorem

records.name: VALUE_ITERATION_CONVERGENCE_COMPLETE
records.statement:
theorem VALUE_ITERATION_CONVERGENCE_COMPLETE (mdp : MDP S A) (γ : Rat)
    (hγ_nonneg : 0 ≤ γ) (hγ_lt : γ < 1) :
    ∃ v_star : S → ℝ,
    -- 1. v_star is the optimal value function (Bellman equation)
    bellmanOperatorReal mdp γ v_star = v_star ∧
    -- 2. Value iteration converges to v_star from any starting point
    (∀ v₀ : S → Rat, Tendsto (fun n => castToReal ((bellmanOperatorRat mdp γ)^[n] v₀)) atTop (𝓝 v_star)) ∧
    -- 3. Geometric convergence with explicit rate
    (∀ v₀ : S → Rat, ∀ n : ℕ,
      dist (castToReal ((bellmanOperatorRat mdp γ)^[n] v₀)) v_star ≤
      dist v₀ (bellmanOperatorRat mdp γ v₀) * γ^n / (1 - γ)) ∧
    -- 4. Uniqueness: any fixed point of the Bellman operator equals v_star
    (∀ v' : S → ℝ, bellmanOperatorReal mdp γ v' = v' → v' = v_star) := by
  sorry
records.doc: **THE MAIN RESULT**: Value iteration converges with all guarantees

records.name: ApproxValueIterationInt.INT_VALUE_ITERATION_APPROX
records.statement:
theorem INT_VALUE_ITERATION_APPROX
    (mdp : MDP S A) (γ : ℚ) (hγ_nonneg : 0 ≤ γ) (hγ_lt : γ < 1) :
    ∃ v_star : S → ℝ,
      bellmanOperatorReal (S:=S) (A:=A) mdp (γ : ℝ) v_star = v_star ∧
      ∀ (v₀ : S → ℤ) (n : ℕ),
        dist (castZtoR ((bellmanOperatorInt (S:=S) (A:=A) mdp γ)^[n] v₀)) v_star
          ≤ (γ : ℝ)^n * dist (castZtoR v₀) v_star +
            ((1 : ℝ) / 2) / (1 - (γ : ℝ)) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
Approximate convergence of integer value iteration.

For discount 0 ≤ γ < 1, the iterate error is bounded by:
  γ^n * dist(v₀, v*) + (1/2) / (1-γ)

records.name: ApproxValueIterationInt.INT_VALUE_ITERATION_EVENTUAL_BALL
records.statement:
theorem INT_VALUE_ITERATION_EVENTUAL_BALL
    (mdp : MDP S A) (γ : ℚ) (hγ_nonneg : 0 ≤ γ) (hγ_lt : γ < 1)
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : ((1 : ℝ) / 2) / (1 - (γ : ℝ)) < ε) :
    ∃ v_star : S → ℝ,
      bellmanOperatorReal (S:=S) (A:=A) mdp (γ : ℝ) v_star = v_star ∧
      ∀ v₀ : S → ℤ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
        dist (castZtoR ((bellmanOperatorInt (S:=S) (A:=A) mdp γ)^[n] v₀)) v_star ≤ ε := by
  sorry
records.doc:
Eventual ball inclusion.

For any ε > (1/2)/(1-γ), the iterates eventually stay within distance ε of v*.

records.name: universal_approximation_cybenko
records.statement:
theorem universal_approximation_cybenko
    (hJD : HasJordanDecomposition n)
    (σ : ℝ → ℝ) (hσ_cont : Continuous σ) (hσ_sig : IsSigmoidal σ)
    (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ) (hf_cont : ContinuousOn f (UnitCube n))
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (w : Fin N → (Fin n → ℝ)) (b : Fin N → ℝ) (α : Fin N → ℝ),
      ∀ x ∈ UnitCube n,
        |f x - neuralNetFun σ N w b α x| < ε := by
  sorry
records.doc: **Cybenko's Universal Approximation Theorem (1989).**

records.name: GaussianMeasure.stdGaussianPi
records.statement:
noncomputable def stdGaussianPi (n : ℕ) : Measure (Fin n → ℝ) :=
  Measure.pi fun _ : Fin n => gaussianReal 0 1
records.doc: Standard Gaussian product measure: the product of n independent standard Gaussians N(0,1)

records.name: GaussianMeasure.stdGaussianE
records.statement:
noncomputable def stdGaussianE (n : ℕ) : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
  Measure.map (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin n) ℝ).symm (stdGaussianPi n)
records.doc: The standard Gaussian on EuclideanSpace as pushforward of stdGaussianPi via the equivalence.

records.name: IsENet
records.statement:
def IsENet {A : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace A] (t : Finset A) (eps : ℝ) (s : Set A) : Prop :=
  s ⊆ ⋃ x ∈ t, closedBall x eps
records.doc:
`t` is an `eps`-net for `s` if every point of `s` lies in a closed ball of radius `eps`
centered at some element of `t`.

records.name: coveringNumber
records.statement:
noncomputable def coveringNumber {A : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace A] (eps : ℝ) (s : Set A) : WithTop Nat :=
  sInf {n : WithTop Nat | ∃ t : Finset A, IsENet t eps s ∧ (t.card : WithTop Nat) = n}
records.doc: Covering number: the minimal cardinality of a finite `eps`-net, as `WithTop Nat`.

records.name: metricEntropyOfNat
records.statement:
def metricEntropyOfNat (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  if n ≤ 1 then 0 else Real.log n
records.doc: Helper to compute metric entropy given a natural number.

records.name: metricEntropy
records.statement:
def metricEntropy (eps : ℝ) (s : Set A) : ℝ :=
  match _h : coveringNumber eps s with
  | ⊤ => 0
  | (n : ℕ) => metricEntropyOfNat n
records.doc: Metric entropy: log of covering number.

records.name: sqrtEntropy
records.statement:
def sqrtEntropy (eps : ℝ) (s : Set A) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt (metricEntropy eps s)
records.doc: Square root of metric entropy.

records.name: dudleyIntegrand
records.statement:
def dudleyIntegrand (eps : ℝ) (s : Set A) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ENNReal.ofReal (sqrtEntropy eps s)
records.doc: Dudley integrand: √(log N(ε, s)) as ENNReal.

records.name: entropyIntegralENNReal
records.statement:
def entropyIntegralENNReal (s : Set A) (D : ℝ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∫⁻ eps in Set.Ioc (0 : ℝ) D, dudleyIntegrand eps s
records.doc: Entropy integral (ENNReal): ∫₀^D √(log N(ε, s)) dε.

records.name: entropyIntegral
records.statement:
def entropyIntegral (s : Set A) (D : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (entropyIntegralENNReal s D).toReal
records.doc: Entropy integral (real-valued wrapper).

records.name: IsSubGaussianProcess
records.doc:
A stochastic process X indexed by a metric space is σ-sub-Gaussian if
the MGF of increments satisfies E[exp(l(X_s - X_t))] ≤ exp(l²σ²d(s,t)²/2).

records.name: EfronSteinApp.CompactlySupportedSmooth
records.statement:
def CompactlySupportedSmooth (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContDiff ℝ 2 f ∧ HasCompactSupport f
records.doc: A function is compactly supported and smooth (C²)

records.name: GaussianLipConcen.gaussian_lipschitz_concentration
records.statement:
theorem gaussian_lipschitz_concentration {f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ} {L : ℝ≥0}
    (hn : 0 < n) (hL : 0 < L) (hf : LipschitzWith L f) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t) :
    let μ := stdGaussianE n
    (μ {x | t ≤ |f x - ∫ y, f y ∂μ|}).toReal ≤ 2 * exp (-t^2 / (2 * (L : ℝ)^2)) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
**Gaussian Lipschitz Concentration Inequality**

For any L-Lipschitz function f on ℝⁿ equipped with the standard Gaussian measure,
the probability that f deviates from its mean by more than t is at most
2 exp(-t² / (2L²)).

records.name: dudley
records.statement:
theorem dudley {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {X : A → Ω → ℝ} {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 0 < σ)
    (hX : IsSubGaussianProcess μ X σ)
    {s : Set A} (hs : TotallyBounded s)
    {D : ℝ} (hD : 0 < D) (hdiam : Metric.diam s ≤ D)
    (t₀ : A) (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ s) (hcenter : ∀ ω, X t₀ ω = 0)
    (hX_meas : ∀ t, Measurable (X t))
    (hX_int_exp : ∀ t s : A, ∀ l : ℝ, Integrable (fun ω => Real.exp (l * (X t ω - X s ω))) μ)
    (hfinite : entropyIntegralENNReal s D ≠ ⊤)
    (hcont : ∀ ω, Continuous (fun (t : ↥s) => X t.1 ω)) :
    ∫ ω, ⨆ t ∈ s, X t ω ∂μ ≤ (12 * Real.sqrt 2) * σ * entropyIntegral s D := by
  sorry
records.doc:
**Dudley's Entropy Integral Theorem**

For a σ-sub-Gaussian process X indexed by a totally bounded set s with diameter ≤ D,
the expected supremum satisfies:
  E[sup_{t∈s} X_t] ≤ 12√2 · σ · ∫₀^D √(log N(ε, s)) dε

records.name: efronStein
records.statement:
theorem efronStein (f : (Fin n → Ω) → ℝ) (hf : MemLp f 2 (Measure.pi μs)) :
    variance f (Measure.pi μs) ≤
    ∑ i : Fin n, ∫ x, (f x - condExpExceptCoord (μs := μs) i f x)^2 ∂(Measure.pi μs) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
**Efron-Stein Inequality**

For independent random variables X₁,...,Xₙ and a square-integrable function f:
  Var(f) ≤ ∑ᵢ E[(f - E^{(i)}f)²]
where E^{(i)}f is the conditional expectation given all variables except Xᵢ.

records.name: GaussianPoincare.gaussianPoincare
records.statement:
theorem gaussianPoincare {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : CompactlySupportedSmooth f) :
    variance (fun x => f x) stdGaussianMeasure ≤
    ∫ x, (deriv f x)^2 ∂stdGaussianMeasure := by
  sorry
records.doc:
**Gaussian Poincaré Inequality**

For any f ∈ C²_c(ℝ) and X ~ N(0,1):
  Var(f(X)) ≤ E[f'(X)²]

records.name: networks_exist
records.statement:
theorem networks_exist (n : ℕ) : ∃ net : ComparatorNetwork n, net.Sorts ∧
    net.depth ≤ 141 * 10 ^ 62 * Nat.clog 2 n ∧
    net.size ≤ 705 * 10 ^ 61 * n * Nat.clog 2 n := by sorry
records.doc: Efficient networks exist

records.name: Problem4.harmonic_mean_inequality_full
records.statement:
theorem harmonic_mean_inequality_full
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (p q : ℝ[X])
    (hp_monic : p.Monic) (hq_monic : q.Monic)
    (hp_deg : p.natDegree = n) (hq_deg : q.natDegree = n)
    (hp_real : ∀ z : ℂ, (p.map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ)).IsRoot z → z.im = 0)
    (hq_real : ∀ z : ℂ, (q.map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ)).IsRoot z → z.im = 0) :
    invPhiN_poly n (polyBoxPlus n p q) ≥ invPhiN_poly n p + invPhiN_poly n q := by sorry
records.doc:
**Main Theorem (Problem 4)**: Harmonic-mean inequality for Φₙ under box-plus
    convolution. For monic real-rooted polynomials p, q of degree n ≥ 2:
    1/Φₙ(p ⊞ₙ q) ≥ 1/Φₙ(p) + 1/Φₙ(q)

records.name: Problem6.exists_eps_light_subset
records.statement:
theorem exists_eps_light_subset
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (ε : ℝ) (hε_pos : 0 < ε) (hε_le : ε ≤ 1) :
    ∃ S : Finset V, IsEpsLight G ε S ∧
      ε / 256 * (Fintype.card V : ℝ) ≤
      (S.card : ℝ) := by sorry
records.doc:
**Main Theorem (Problem 6)**: For every simple graph G on a finite vertex set V
    and every ε ∈ (0, 1], there exists an ε-light subset S with |S| ≥ ε/256 · |V|.

records.name: Zip.Native.Deflate.inflate_deflateRaw
records.statement:
theorem inflate_deflateRaw (data : ByteArray) (level : UInt8)
    (maxOutputSize : Nat) (hsize : data.size < maxOutputSize) :
    Zip.Native.Inflate.inflate (deflateRaw data level) maxOutputSize = .ok data := by
  sorry
records.doc:
Unified DEFLATE roundtrip: inflate ∘ deflateRaw = identity.
    Generalized to any `maxOutputSize` large enough to hold the input.

records.name: Zip.Native.Deflate.deflateRaw_pad
records.statement:
theorem deflateRaw_pad (data : ByteArray) (level : UInt8) :
    ∃ (contentBits padding : List Bool),
      Deflate.Spec.bytesToBits (deflateRaw data level) = contentBits ++ padding ∧
      padding.length < 8 := by
  sorry
records.doc:
The output of `deflateRaw` decomposes into content bits plus short padding.
    Needed by `inflateRaw_endPos_ge` to establish that the native decoder
    consumes all of the deflated byte array.

records.name: Zip.Native.Deflate.deflateRaw_goR_pad
records.statement:
theorem deflateRaw_goR_pad (data : ByteArray) (level : UInt8) :
    ∃ remaining,
      Deflate.Spec.decode.goR (Deflate.Spec.bytesToBits (deflateRaw data level)) []
        = some (data.data.toList, remaining) ∧ remaining.length < 8 := by
  sorry
records.doc:
For the encoder's output, `decode.goR` returns a short remaining (< 8 bits).
    Connects encoder structure to decoder bit consumption.

records.name: AgreeToDisagree.agreeToDisagree
records.doc: Formalizes Aumann's agreement theorem for information partitions and a common-prior setting, together with a p-belief variant bounding posterior disagreement by 2 * (1 - p).

records.name: MeasureTheory.Lp_Burkholder_inequality_martingaleTransform
records.doc: Formalizes Burkholder's sharp Lp inequality for real-valued martingale transforms: if `f` is a discrete martingale and `w` a predictable multiplier bounded by `1`, then the Lp norm of the transform `w ⋆ₘ f` is at most `(pStar p - 1)` times the Lp norm of `f`, where `pStar p` is the maximum of `p` and its conjugate exponent. The proof builds the Burkholder special function as a majorant of the relevant payoff in each exponent regime (`1 < p < 2`, `p = 2`, `p > 2`).
records.informal: The sharp Lp Burkholder inequality: for a discrete martingale `f` and a predictable multiplier `w` with `|w n| ≤ 1`, the Lp norm of the martingale transform `(w ⋆ₘ f) n` is bounded by `(pStar p - 1)` times the Lp norm of `f n`.

The proof builds the Burkholder special function as a majorant of the relevant payoff in each exponent regime (`1 < p < 2`, `p = 2`, `p > 2`).

records.name: ChannelCapacity.exists_unique_capacity_achieving_prior_of_finite
records.doc: Formalizes uniqueness of the capacity-achieving input distribution for a Markov-kernel channel in three aligned layers: a finite-alphabet theorem (compactness, continuity, and strict concavity of mutual information on Mathlib's weak topology for `ProbabilityMeasure`), a concrete discharged theorem for compact-Polish channels with a common strictly positive jointly continuous density, and a general measure-theoretic packaging that isolates the abstract well-conditioning hypotheses, plus a counterexample showing pairwise-distinct rows do not give an injective prior pushforward (the non-degeneracy required for uniqueness).

records.name: Chudnovsky.chudnovskySum_eq_pi_inv
records.entry_name: A Detailed Proof of the Chudnovsky Formula
records.doc: Formalizes the Chudnovsky brothers' rapidly convergent series for 1/π, proving Mathlib's `chudnovskySum = π⁻¹`. Follows Milla's elementary complex-analytic proof: Weierstrass and Eisenstein theory, Liouville and parallelogram-residue calculus, the Kummer hypergeometric bridge and the main modular identity relating the j-invariant to the lattice periods, Baker's division-value machinery, and the singular-moduli inputs at the CM point τ = (1 + √-163)/2 — integrality of j(τ) via modular polynomials and Kronecker's congruence, and rationality of the Weierstrass s₂ invariant via Masser's Appendix A.1.
records.informal: Proves the Chudnovsky series identity, i.e. Mathlib's `chudnovskySum = π⁻¹`: the series (12 / 640320^(3/2)) · ∑ₙ (-1)ⁿ (6n)! (545140134 n + 13591409) / ((3n)! (n!)³ 640320^(3n)) sums to 1/π.

records.entry_name: Spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators
records.doc: Formalizes the spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space: such an operator admits a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors. records.informal: A compact self-adjoint operator has an eigenvector whose eigenvalue realizes either the supremum or the infimum of its Rayleigh quotient.

records.entry_name: Spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators
records.doc: Formalizes the spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space: such an operator admits a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors. The development passes from weak compactness of Hilbert closed balls and Rayleigh-quotient extrema to an eigenvector at the operator norm, finiteness of the point spectrum outside any neighbourhood of zero, finite-rank cutoff approximation, and finally the orthogonal decomposition into eigenspaces.
records.informal: The set of nonzero eigenvalues of a compact self-adjoint operator is countable.

records.name: CompositionAlgebra.hurwitz_classification
records.entry_name: Hurwitz's Classification of Euclidean Composition Algebras
records.doc: Formalizes Hurwitz's classification of nontrivial finite-dimensional real Euclidean composition algebras: every such algebra has dimension 1, 2, 4, or 8 and is real-linearly equivalent to the real numbers, complex numbers, quaternions, or octonions through a map preserving the unit, multiplication, and norm form. The development also constructs the octonions from an explicit Fano multiplication table, proves Degen's eight-square identity, and shows that Cayley--Dickson doubling preserves the composition law for associative inputs.
records.informal: Every nontrivial finite-dimensional real Euclidean composition algebra is linearly equivalent to the real numbers, complex numbers, quaternions, or octonions through a map preserving the unit, multiplication, and norm form.

records.name: CutAndProject.main_theorem_geometric_concrete
records.entry_name: Period Lengths of Rational Cut-and-Project Gap Sequences
records.doc: Formalizes the closed-form minimal periods of one-dimensional rational cut-and-project gap sequences at the level of the paper's residue model, plus a fully geometric aperiodicity theorem for irrational slopes. For coprime α, β ∈ ℕ and window parameter ω ≥ 0, write N = ⌊ωα⌋ + ⌊ωβ⌋ + 1 and D = α² + β². The strip-to-residue reduction of the paper — sorting the hits of the length-N progression twisted by the geometric multiplier −αβ⁻¹ (mod D) — is taken as the definition of the gap sequence rather than derived from the lattice; for it, the multiset convention has minimal period N/D when D ∣ N and N otherwise, and the set convention (multiplicities flattened to {0,1}) has minimal period 1 when N ≥ D and N otherwise. The irrational case is geometric from first principles: for positive irrational slope and ω > 0, the accepted points of ℤ² sorted by the physical projection have a gap sequence with no finite period, via injectivity of the projection and Kronecker density of the internal image.
records.informal: The gap sequence of the residue model of the rational cut-and-project multiset (sorted hits of the length-N progression under the multiplier −αβ⁻¹ mod D) has minimal period N/D if D divides N and N otherwise, where N = ⌊ωα⌋ + ⌊ωβ⌋ + 1 and D = α² + β².

records.name: Basic.ProjectiveGeometry

records.name: DistanceGeometry.schoenberg
records.doc: Develops the basepoint-centered Gram approach to finite Euclidean distance geometry. Proves both directions of Schoenberg's characterization, including a rank-controlled factorization of positive-semidefinite matrices; proves that three affinely independent centers in Euclidean three-space determine at most two points with prescribed distances; and verifies the Cayley--Menger determinant for segments and triangles, including the triangle-area identity underlying Heron's formula.
records.informal: For n at least one, a symmetric hollow n-by-n matrix is a squared-distance matrix of points in k-dimensional Euclidean space exactly when its basepoint-centered Gram matrix is positive semidefinite and has rank at most k.

records.informal: Three affinely independent centers in three-dimensional Euclidean space admit at most two points with any prescribed triple of distances.

records.name: Erdos97Octagon.erdos97_convex_octagon
records.entry_name: The Convex-Octagon Case of Erdős Problem 97
records.doc: Proves that among eight labelled points in the Euclidean plane in convex position, at least one point has no four other points at a common distance. The development reduces a geometric counterexample to a finite incidence model, classifies normalized row patterns up to symmetry, proves geometric and algebraic obstructions, and excludes seven canonical first-row masks with a kernel-audited exhaustive search over the remaining legal row masks and checked geometric obstruction witnesses. This is the modern four-equidistant formulation; Erdős's 1946 paper posed the stronger three-equidistant version. This is the convex-octagon case only; the general Erdős Problem 97 remains open.
records.informal: Among eight labelled points in the Euclidean plane in convex position, some point has no four other points at a common distance.

records.name: LeanPool.ErdosMoser.leoMoserVarianceBound
records.doc: Formalizes the exact finite sum-of-squares inequality that Guy's 1982 account states as Theorem 2 and attributes to Leo Moser: a finite set A of natural numbers with distinct subset sums satisfies 4^|A| - 1 <= 3 * sum(a^2). It then derives direct and square-root lower bounds for the largest element of A. This does not claim the stronger historical asymptotic bound attributed jointly to Erdős and Moser, and Erdős Problem 1 remains open.
records.informal: If a finite set A of natural numbers has distinct subset sums, then 4^|A| - 1 is at most three times the sum of the squares of the elements of A.

records.name: LeanPool.Erdos132ConvexK3.convex_top_three_degree_six
records.entry_name: Convex Three-Distance Degree-Six Theorem and Exceptional-Word Closures
records.doc: Proves that every finite cyclically strictly convex planar configuration has a vertex incident to at most six edges from its three largest distance classes. The proof selects a maximal-gap vertex and coordinated majorants, closes all exceptional inner branches, performs the five-row enumeration, and transports all thirteen canonical cover words to four shared full-two-rung, anti-saturation, terminal-cage, and four-edge-cage predicates. It also proves exceptional-count rigidity and an explicit heptagon refutation of a tempting stronger majorant claim, with rational regression witnesses. This settles the all-n k=3 instance of the paper's suggested degree-2k convex bound; Morić--Pritchard proved the corresponding top-three edge bound for sufficiently large n. It does not settle the general-k suggestion or the general Erdős problem 132.
records.informal: For every nonempty finite cyclically strictly convex planar configuration with three strictly ordered largest squared-distance classes d₁, d₂, and d₃, some vertex is incident to at most six pairs whose squared distance is one of those three classes.

records.name: LeanPool.Erdos132N14.erdos132_for_fourteen_of_published_inputs

records.doc: Formalizes the planar Hopf--Pannwitz diameter bound and proves the fourteen-point low-multiplicity conclusion conditional on exactly two remaining published interfaces: the known maximum-cardinality bound for planar sets with at most six distances and the Szöllősi--Östergård classification of thirteen-point planar six-distance sets. Internally derives the exact failure profile and endpoint deletion, constructs the three classified templates, eliminates the nonregular cases by multiplicity, and excludes the regular tridecagon extension by explicit second and fourth moments. The general Erdős problem remains open.
records.informal: Assuming precisely the published planar few-distance cardinality and Szöllősi--Östergård classification interfaces, every injectively labelled fourteen-point planar configuration realizes at least two distances whose unordered-pair multiplicities are at most fourteen.

records.name: Erdos132ThreeChain.nonDiameterSqDists_ne_chain
records.entry_name: Planar Point Sets Whose Non-Diameter Distances Form a Geometric 3-Chain
records.doc:
Formalizes a support theorem about planar point sets whose non-diameter squared distances are confined to a geometric progression of ratio three. The chain-quadruple theorem shows that no planar quadruple with all six squared distances in such a chain can span two chain steps, and classifies the seven labelled patterns that do occur: the rhombus of two glued equilateral triangles, in five positions of its long edge, and the equilateral triangle with its centroid, in two. records.informal: Let n be at least thirteen, let a be positive, and let X be a finite set of points of the real plane with exactly n elements. Suppose D is the squared diameter of X, meaning that D is realised by two distinct points of X and dominates every squared distance inside X. Then for every natural number h, the set of squared distances realised by distinct points of X and different from D is not equal to the geometric 3-chain consisting of a times 3^j for j below h.

Then each of the four squared distances from A and B to C and to D equals c or 3c, at least one of the two squared distances from A and B to C equals c, likewise for D, the squared distance from C to D equals c or 3c, the squared distance from A to C equals c or that from B to D equals c, the squared distance from B to C equals c or that from A to D equals c, and the whole labelling is one of exactly seven explicit patterns: five with a single edge of squared length 3c, and two in which the three edges of squared length 3c form a triangle.

records.name: Erdos137.erdos137_finite
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem #137: powerful products of consecutive integers
records.doc: Formalizes the abc-conditional finiteness results for Erdős Problem #137 (Erdős–Selfridge): a number N is powerful if every prime dividing N has its square dividing N, and the question is whether the product F(k,n) = n(n+1)⋯(n+k-1) of k ≥ 3 consecutive integers can be powerful for infinitely many n. Each route isolates its abc input (a radical lower bound) as a single explicit hypothesis and proves everything else outright, concluding that, conditionally, F(k,n) is powerful for only finitely many n for each fixed k ≥ 3.
records.informal: Under the Granville–Langevin radical bound RadLB k (an abc-conditional hypothesis) and k ≥ 3, the set of n ≥ 1 for which F(k,n) is powerful is finite.

records.name: Erdos137.erdos137_eventually_not_powerful
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem #137: powerful products of consecutive integers

Each route isolates its abc input (a radical lower bound) as a single explicit hypothesis and proves everything else outright, concluding that, conditionally, F(k,n) is powerful for only finitely many n for each fixed k ≥ 3.
records.informal: Under RadLB k and k ≥ 3, there is a threshold beyond which F(k,n) is never powerful.

records.name: Erdos346.intended_problem_if_limit_exists
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 346: Ratio Limit Forces the Golden Ratio
records.doc: Formalizes the limit-exists interpretation of Erdős Problem 346: for a strictly increasing positive integer sequence with a uniform ratio gap whose finite deletions are complete but whose infinite deletions are not, if the consecutive quotient sequence converges to some real limit greater than one, then that limit must equal the golden ratio and the quotient sequence tends to it.
records.informal: Existence of any limit greater than one for the quotient sequence forces convergence to the golden ratio, the intended Erdős–Graham conclusion.

records.informal: If the quotient sequence converges to a limit greater than one under the completeness and incompleteness deletion hypotheses, that limit equals the golden ratio.

records.name: Erdos403.erdos_403_sharp
records.entry_name: Sums of Distinct Factorials That Are Powers of Two (Erdos Problem 403)
records.doc: Reconstructs the finiteness theorem for Erdos Problem 403: only finitely many sums of distinct factorials are powers of two, and every such power is at most 2^7 = 128 (the extremal solution 2! + 3! + 5! = 128). records.name: Erdos865.erdos865_upper_bound
records.entry_name: A sharp 5/8 bound for Erdős Problem 865
records.doc: Formalizes the resolution of Erdős Problem 865 on pairwise sums. For A ⊆ {1,…,N}, a pairwise-sum triple is a set of distinct a, b, c ∈ A with a+b, a+c, b+c all in A, and A is triple-free when it has none. The development proves that every triple-free A ⊆ [1,N] satisfies 8·|A| ≤ 5·N + 53, that any A exceeding this bound contains a triple, and — via the construction A = [M,2M] ∪ [4M,8M] for N = 8M — that the constant 5/8 is optimal, so f₃(N) = 5N/8 + O(1). The upper bound runs through a folded additive lemma over ℤ/mℤ (a four-set union bound) and a folding lemma, closed by strong induction on N.
records.informal: Every triple-free set A ⊆ [1,N] satisfies 8·|A| ≤ 5·N + 53, i.e. |A| ≤ (5/8)·N + O(1).

records.name: Feige.sharp_unit_slack_feige_complete
records.doc: For small-universe probability spaces, proves the sharp fixed-dimensional unit-slack lower bound for sums of independent nonnegative random variables: if each coordinate has mean at most one, then the probability that the sum lies below its mean plus one is at least (n/(n+1))^n, and this constant is optimal. records.name: GKPCarry.tendsto_gkpSuccessProportion_one
records.entry_name: Density-One GKP Divisibility and Its Carry-Language Characterization
records.doc: Proves that the exponents k satisfying the Graham--Knuth--Patashnik divisibility condition have natural density one. The proof gives an exact all-depth modular sieve, quantitative bounds for possible failures in initial intervals, and a density-zero limit for the failure proportion. It also develops the Kummer digit-sum bridge, the binary-popcount reduction, and a verified ternary carry automaton. The universal GKP conjecture remains open because the possible density-zero failure set may be nonempty.
records.informal: The proportion of exponents k below N for which nine divides the central binomial coefficient indexed by 2^k tends to one as N tends to infinity.

records.name: HadwigerNelsonBounds.hadwiger_nelson_known_bounds
records.entry_name: Known Bounds for the Hadwiger-Nelson Problem
records.doc: Formalizes the currently known bounds 5 <= chi(R^2) <= 7 for the chromatic number of the Euclidean plane. The upper bound constructs an explicit Isbell-style seven-coloring. The lower bound checks Parts' 481-vertex coloring certificate, develops a finite doubled triangular-lattice forcing gadget, proves its exact Euclidean embedding, and closes the four-color contradiction with a spindle construction. The exact chromatic number remains open.
records.informal: The chromatic number of the unit-distance graph on the Euclidean plane lies between five and seven, inclusive.

records.name: LeanPool.HansonWright.hanson_wright_inequality_hdp
records.entry_name: The Hanson-Wright inequality for sub-Gaussian quadratic forms
records.doc: Proves the finite-dimensional Hanson-Wright concentration inequality for quadratic forms of independent mean-zero sub-Gaussian real random variables whose maximum least global-MGF sub-Gaussian scale is positive, for matrices with positive Frobenius and operator norms. The bound uses the fixed universal coefficient 1 / (256 * exp(1)^2). This is the MGF normalization of the usual result; no formal identification with an Orlicz psi-2 norm is claimed. The development derives the required moment-generating-function certificate instead of assuming it, and contributes reusable scalar Bernstein, Chernoff, cumulant, sub-Gaussian-process, and finite-maximum infrastructure.
records.informal: For independent mean-zero real random variables with finite least global-MGF sub-Gaussian scales and positive maximum coordinate MGF scale, and a matrix with positive Frobenius and operator norms, the centered quadratic form satisfies the Hanson-Wright two-regime exponential tail bound with the fixed universal coefficient 1 / (256 * exp(1)^2).

records.name: IsoGraph.Canon.canonAdj_eq_iff
records.entry_name: Verified canonical labelling of finite graphs
records.doc: Implements an individualisation-refinement canonical-labelling algorithm in the style of nauty and proves that its canonical adjacency form is invariant under vertex relabelling and classifies finite graphs up to isomorphism. records.name: genus_eq_zero_iff_homeo
records.entry_name: The Jacobian of a Compact Riemann Surface
records.doc: Constructs the Jacobian of a compact Riemann surface as the period-lattice quotient of the dual of holomorphic 1-forms, and proves the surrounding theory it needs: the genus as the dimension of the space of holomorphic 1-forms, discreteness and full rank 2g of the period lattice, the Abel-Jacobi map and its injectivity in positive genus, functoriality (pushforward, pullback, degree, and the projection formula), Riemann-Roch, Serre duality via Laurent tails, the residue theorem, the Dolbeault-Cech comparison, and finite dimensionality of the first cohomology by a Schwartz/Montel argument. The headline no-hack guard is that the genus vanishes exactly when the surface is homeomorphic to the sphere.
records.informal: A compact connected Riemann surface has genus zero if and only if it is homeomorphic to the 2-sphere.

records.name: JL.johnson_lindenstrauss
records.entry_name: The Johnson–Lindenstrauss Lemma and Quantized JL
records.doc: Formalizes the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma end to end — a Gaussian random projection preserves pairwise distances of a finite point set up to a (1 ± ε) factor, so a distortion-ε embedding of any m-point set exists once k is logarithmic in m — together with the quantized JL (QJL) one-bit sign sketch: unbiasedness of the asymmetric 1-bit estimator and its sub-Gaussian distortion bound.
records.informal: The abstract probabilistic-method union bound — if the summed per-pair distortion-failure probability is below one, a distortion-preserving map exists.

records.name: KahnKalai.covering_theorem
records.doc: Formalizes Tran and Vu's short proof of the Park–Pham theorem resolving the Kahn–Kalai expectation-threshold conjecture. For an ℓ-bounded family of subsets of a finite ground set, it proves the strengthened covering theorem with the explicit constant L = 1000 and derives the threshold bound p_c(F) ≤ K q(F) log₂ ℓ with the explicit witness K = 100000. The supporting library develops finite-set cover cost, level-density, double-counting, binomial-tail, and numeric estimates.
records.informal: If ℓ ≤ N, p lies in [0, 1], and an ℓ-bounded family H has cover cost at least 1/2 - 2^(-(ℓ+2)), then its upset has at least (2/3 + 2^(-(ℓ+2))) choose(N, m) members of cardinality m, where m = floor(1000 p N log₂(ℓ+1)). For m ≤ N this is the corresponding level-density bound; for N < m both cardinalities are zero.

records.informal: There is an absolute positive constant K such that every ℓ-bounded finite family with ℓ at least two satisfies p_c(F) ≤ K q(F) log₂ ℓ; the proof supplies K = 100000.

records.name: KasamiCyclicAdditive.carlet_kasami_cyclic_additive_literature
records.doc: Proves Carlet's cyclic-additive conjecture for the Kasami power function: over every finite field of characteristic two with cardinality 2^n and every k coprime to n, the normalized derivative image has the exact coefficient triple count 2^(2n-3) for all distinct nonzero slopes. The development combines the Müller--Cohen--Matthews permutation theorem, multiplicative character sums, Fourier inversion, and a Fermat-cubic Frobenius-kernel argument.
records.informal: For every finite field K of characteristic two with |K| = 2^n, every k coprime to n, and all distinct nonzero v₁ and v₂ in K, the coefficient triple count of the normalized Kasami derivative image is exactly 2^(2n-3).

records.name: KrafftSieve.mu_min_lt_one_implies_tpc
records.entry_name: A Conditional Sieve Criterion for Twin Primes via Krafft Geometry
records.doc: Introduces an original conditional sieve criterion for the Twin Prime Conjecture. Using a centered modular alignment (termed the Krafft alignment), proves that if the Rayleigh-Ritz quotient over the orthogonal unit sphere satisfies muMin < 1, then a twin prime pair must exist in the corresponding interval.
records.informal: If there are infinitely many intervals where the optimal multidimensional weight achieves a ratio strictly less than 1, then there are infinitely many twin primes. This is a conditional reduction; the hypothesis muMin n < 1 is not established here for any n.

records.name: LehmerE10.main_theorem
records.entry_name: Lehmer's Polynomial and the E10 Coxeter Element
records.doc: Proves that Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial — the integer polynomial of smallest known Mahler measure above 1 — is irreducible over the integers, and that it is the characteristic polynomial of a Coxeter element of the E10 Weyl group (the rank-10 instance of McMullen). Against Mathlib's Mahler-measure API it computes M(L) exactly as the Salem root with the unconditional bounds 1 < M(L) < 7/5, states Lehmer's conjecture as a defined Prop (never assumed) with the strong form implying the gap form, and contrasts the E8 Coxeter element (order exactly 30) with the E10 element (infinite order in GL(10,Z)): the E-series crosses from torsion to a Salem matrix at rank 10, and the crossing value is Lehmer's number.
records.informal: Lehmer's polynomial L(x) = x^10 + x^9 - x^7 - x^6 - x^5 - x^4 - x^3 + x + 1 is irreducible over the integers, and the characteristic polynomial of a Coxeter element of the E10 Weyl group equals L.

records.informal: The Mahler measure of L equals its Salem root mu, with the unconditional bounds 1 < M(L) < 7/5.

records.name: LongGapsBetweenPrimes.long_prime_gaps
records.entry_name: Improved long gaps between consecutive primes
records.doc: Formalizes the unconditional lower bound showing that, for all sufficiently large X, the largest gap between consecutive primes below X is at least a positive constant times log X (log log X)^2 log log log log X / (log log log X)^2. The development includes the short-translates sieve proposition, divisor coefficient estimates, truncated product weights, moment bounds, and the Erdos--Rankin covering argument used to derive the headline result.
records.informal: There are a positive constant c and a real threshold X0 such that for every X at least X0, some pair of consecutive indexed primes below X has gap greater than c times log X (log log X)^2 log log log log X / (log log log X)^2.

records.name: LeanPool.MoserLatticeColorings.MoserRing.both_colorings_are_geometric
records.entry_name: Geometric Four-Colorings of the Moser Lattice and Ring
records.doc: Formalizes the two explicit parity colorings from Dúcz's 2026 note on the Moser lattice. The development derives the exact quadratic norm formula, proves that the integer-coordinate embedding is faithful, proves both colorings proper and geometric on the entire lattice, and descends them through localization by powers of three to the Moser ring. As a structural corollary, every unit-distance graph realized entirely in the Moser ring is four-colorable. The uniqueness classification of geometric four-colorings and the chromatic number of the full Euclidean plane are not claimed.
records.informal: The two parity maps defined by Dúcz descend to proper four-colorings of the full Moser ring, and equality of colors for each map depends only on Euclidean distance.

records.name: OddPrimeValuationDistribution.oddPrimeValuationGeneratingSeries_identity
records.entry_name: Exact odd-prime distributions of central-binomial valuations
records.doc: Formalizes the exact distribution of the p-adic valuation of the central binomial coefficient binom(2n,n) over every complete block 0 <= n < p^k for every odd prime p. The development proves Kummer correctness for padded digit words, constructs the two-state doubling carry enumerator, identifies it with the arithmetic valuation polynomial, derives its second-order recurrence, proves the rational bivariate generating function, and obtains closed formulas for valuations zero and one.
records.informal: For every odd prime p = 2h+1, proves the denominator-cleared identity for the bivariate series whose coefficient of T^k X^r counts n < p^k with nu_p(binomial(2n,n)) = r; equivalently the series is (1-XT)/(1-(h+1)(1+X)T+pXT^2).

records.name: PebblingLean.Hypercube.Paper.optimalPebblingNumber_theta

records.doc: Formalizes that the optimal pebbling number of the n-dimensional hypercube Q_n is Theta((4/3)^n).  Builds a weight-function lower bound of (4/3)^n and a probabilistic recursive upper bound C * (4/3)^n with an explicit constant, combining them into a two-sided big-Theta witness.

records.name: LeanPool.PoincareThreeBody.nonintegrability_of_collisionBand
records.entry_name: Poincaré's Nonintegrability Theorem for the Restricted Three-Body Problem
records.doc: Formalizes Poincaré's classical parameter-analytic nonintegrability theorem for the planar circular restricted three-body problem. The development defines the rotating-frame Hamiltonian on its collision-free domain, proves logarithmic blow-up of the resonant disturbing average at an apoapsis collision boundary, and analytically propagates the resulting dense resonant obstruction to exclude an additional analytic first integral. The final statement is the fixed-coordinate, global uniform-domain special case of the planar part of Yagasaki's Theorem 1.1; his local meromorphic resonant-orbit obstruction is Theorem 3.1.
records.informal: No jointly real-analytic family near zero mass can be an additional first integral of the planar circular restricted three-body Hamiltonian with phase differential independent from the Hamiltonian differential anywhere on the uniform collision-free domain.

records.name: QuadraticIterates.section3_main
records.entry_name: Galois groups of quadratic polynomial iterates
records.doc: Formalizes Stoll's criterion for when the Galois group of the n-th iterate of X² + a over the rationals is the full n-fold iterated wreath product of C₂. It proves the criterion in terms of two-independence of a signed critical-orbit sequence and its pairwise-coprime Möbius factors, and derives the paper's congruence families for which maximality holds at every level. The supporting library develops reusable multiquadratic-extension, iterated wreath-product, Möbius-factor, and valuation results.
records.informal: The Galois group is the full iterated wreath product at every positive level when a is positive and congruent to 1 or 2 modulo 4, or when a is negative and divisible by 4 with -a nonsquare.

records.name: QuadraticIterates.section1_equiv

It proves the criterion in terms of two-independence of a signed critical-orbit sequence and its pairwise-coprime Möbius factors, and derives the paper's congruence families for which maximality holds at every level. The supporting library develops reusable multiquadratic-extension, iterated wreath-product, Möbius-factor, and valuation results.
records.informal: For each n, assuming -a is not a rational square, the Galois group of the n-th iterate of X² + a is the full n-fold iterated wreath product of C₂ exactly when either the first n terms of the signed sequence c₁ = -a, cₖ = fₖ(0) for k ≥ 2, or the first n integer Möbius factors of that sequence are independent modulo rational squares.

records.name: Sabidussi.LoopMultigraph.loop_sabidussi_compatibility_ordinary
records.entry_name: Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture for Eulerian multigraphs
records.doc: Formalizes Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture for finite labelled endpoint multigraphs with loops and parallel edges, where a loop contributes two half-edge incidences to the degree of its vertex. Given an Euler tour and minimum degree at least four, the main theorem constructs a partition of all edges into nonempty, edge-connected, 2-regular ordinary circuits such that consecutive edges of the Euler tour never lie in the same circuit. The proof runs a four-colour (F_2^2) algebra over the cyclic transition word, uses an odd balancing parity lemma to choose compatible local frames, and transports the resulting colouring back to a compatible ordinary circuit decomposition.
records.informal: For any finite endpoint multigraph with an Euler tour and minimum degree at least four, the edges partition into ordinary, nonempty, connected, 2-regular circuits that are compatible with the tour: no circuit contains two consecutive tour edges.

records.name: LeanStationaryHarmonicMaps.StationaryHarmonicMap.StationaryW12LocMap
records.entry_name: Monotonicity Formula for Stationary Harmonic Maps
records.doc: Formalizes the monotonicity formula for stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` maps with Euclidean target. The proof is target independent: it uses only the displayed weak gradient and a vanishing domain first variation, so no target-manifold structure enters the argument. From a bundled stationary Sobolev witness `StationaryW12LocMap u Omega` it proves, for `0 < s <= r < R0`, that the normalized energy `Theta(Du, a, rho) = rho^(2-n) * integral over B(a, rho) of |Du|^2` is monotone: `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r`, together with the exact increment formula `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r`. The Sobolev layer is project-defined from Mathlib's `MemLp`, weak-derivative identities, Bochner integration, and Euclidean measure theory, following the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser engineering choice; the internal proof routes through a radial vector-field first variation, a coarea/Radon-Nikodym radius representation, smooth radial cutoffs, and an absolute-continuity boundary step.
records.informal: The public input package: a domain-variation stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` Sobolev map bundling a chosen weak gradient (`W12LocMapWitness`) with the vanishing domain first-variation identity. This is the object users construct to invoke the monotonicity theorem.

records.doc: Formalizes the three-gap (Steinhaus, three-distance) theorem: for every real `a` and every `N`, the `N`-point orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` partitions `[0,1)` into gaps taking at most three distinct lengths, and when exactly three occur the largest is the sum of the other two. records.entry_name: Ulm's theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups
records.doc: Formalizes Ulm's classification theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups in arbitrary Lean universes. The development constructs the transfinite Ulm filtration and invariants, proves their invariance under additive equivalence, establishes Kaplansky's one-generator extension lemma, and completes the countable back-and-forth classification. records.informal: For any prime p and any two countable reduced abelian p-groups in the same arbitrary Lean universe, the groups are additively isomorphic if and only if all of their classical Ulm invariants, indexed by universe-zero ordinals, agree.

records.name: SendovConjecture.sendov
records.doc: A Lean formalization of Sendov's conjecture, and of its Phelps-Rodriguez strengthening, in full generality: if every zero of a complex polynomial p of degree n >= 2 lies in the closed unit disk, then every zero a of p has a critical point of p within distance 1 of it, and within distance strictly less than 1 unless |a| = 1 and p is a scalar multiple of z^n - a^n. The proof is by contradiction. Degrees 2 to 4 fall to an elementary integral computation; degree 5 upward goes through two estimates on the same integral -- a polar channel and an origin channel -- which are shown to be incompatible, reducing the theorem to a single numerical inequality. That inequality is discharged by exact rational Bernstein certificates, generated outside Lean and re-verified inside it, in both of its ranges: per-degree certificates for 5 <= n <= 100, and, for n >= 101, a single degree-58 certificate closing the one-variable inequality that the analytic large-degree reduction leaves behind. The boundary case |a| = 1 is proved separately from a reciprocal identity, and it is there that the equality classification is extracted. Nothing here is claimed to be new: the informal proof being formalized is a digestion of Lech Mazur's proof, which had already been formalized in Lean, so this is a second and independently checkable machine-checked proof of Sendov's conjecture, whose additional content is the Phelps-Rodriguez equality case. The Lean source was written by an AI agent under the direction and review of the author. There is no sorry outside the two deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, no native_decide, and no floating point in any statement or proof.

records.name: SendovConjecture.phelps_rodriguez
records.doc: A Lean formalization of Sendov's conjecture, and of its Phelps-Rodriguez strengthening, in full generality: if every zero of a complex polynomial p of degree n >= 2 lies in the closed unit disk, then every zero a of p has a critical point of p within distance 1 of it, and within distance strictly less than 1 unless |a| = 1 and p is a scalar multiple of z^n - a^n. The proof is by contradiction. Degrees 2 to 4 fall to an elementary integral computation; degree 5 upward goes through two estimates on the same integral -- a polar channel and an origin channel -- which are shown to be incompatible, reducing the theorem to a single numerical inequality. That inequality is discharged by exact rational Bernstein certificates, generated outside Lean and re-verified inside it, in both of its ranges: per-degree certificates for 5 <= n <= 100, and, for n >= 101, a single degree-58 certificate closing the one-variable inequality that the analytic large-degree reduction leaves behind. The boundary case |a| = 1 is proved separately from a reciprocal identity, and it is there that the equality classification is extracted. Nothing here is claimed to be new: the informal proof being formalized is a digestion of Lech Mazur's proof, which had already been formalized in Lean, so this is a second and independently checkable machine-checked proof of Sendov's conjecture, whose additional content is the Phelps-Rodriguez equality case. The Lean source was written by an AI agent under the direction and review of the author. There is no sorry outside the two deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, no native_decide, and no floating point in any statement or proof.

records.name: NUS.m_lower_bound
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that there are absolute constants c > 0 and p₀ such that, for every prime p ≥ p₀, the minimum size m(p) of a set A ⊆ 𝔽_p with |A| ≥ 2 and no uniquely represented sum satisfies m(p) ≥ c (log p / log log p)².  Here representations are unordered two-element multisets from A, repeated summands are allowed, and "no unique sum" means that every such multiset has a distinct equal-sum mate.

records.name: jordan_curve
records.doc: The Jordan curve theorem, formalized in Lean 4 against Mathlib: a continuous injective map from the circle into the plane has a complement with exactly two connected components. The hypothesis is bare continuity and injectivity — no smoothness, piecewise-linearity or rectifiability — which is what makes the theorem hard and what separates it from the polygonal case. The proof follows Maehara's reduction to the Brouwer fixed point theorem, via a crossing lemma for transversal paths in a rectangle and the fact that every component has the curve as its boundary, together with a farthest-pair normalization that pins down exactly one bounded component. Because Mathlib has no Brouwer fixed point theorem at the pinned revision, Brouwer is built here from the ground up: covering-space path lifting for the circle giving π₁(S¹) ≅ ℤ, then no-retraction of the disk onto its boundary, then Brouwer on the disk by ray-retraction, then the general nonempty-compact-convex case by nearest-point projection. The statement is expressed in Mathlib's own vocabulary. The proof is sorry-free and depends on Lean's three standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) and nothing else.

records.name: erdos501_closed_infinite
records.doc: Erdős problem #501 (Erdős 1961; Erdős–Hajnal 1971, Problem 38): for every real x let A_x be a bounded set of reals of Lebesgue outer measure < 1; must there be an infinite independent set, i.e. an infinite X ⊆ ℝ with x ∉ A_y for all distinct x, y ∈ X?  And if the sets A_x are closed of measure < 1, must there be an independent set of size 3?  This repository formalizes both answers.  Second question: yes — closed sets of measure < 1 admit an infinite independent set (Newelski–Pawlikowski–Seredyński 1987; no boundedness is needed), hence one of size 3.  First question: independent of ZFC.  Under CH (as ℵ₁ = 𝔠) Hechler's 1972 construction gives a family of bounded sets of outer measure < 1 (in fact countable and null) with no infinite independent set — a Mathlib-level theorem — and the negation of the first question holds in the Boolean-valued model of the collapse algebra Col(ω₁, 𝒫(ω)); after adding 𝔠⁺ random reals (Glazer and Sol 2026, adapting the paper's ω₂ random reals over a CH ground) the first question has a positive answer, so it holds in the Boolean-valued model of the random algebra with 𝔠⁺ coordinates.  Both Boolean-valued models are built in a Lean 4 port of Han–van Doorn's Flypitch (the framework of their independence-of-CH proof), and Flypitch's completeness theorem turns them into two-valued models.  The comparator challenge states the results in Mathlib alone: the language of set theory, the theory ZFC (Flypitch's axiomatization: extensionality, empty set, ordered pairs, union, power set, infinity, regularity, Zorn's lemma, strong collection) and the sentence Erdos501 ("every complete ordered field has the Erdős property") are defined in Mathlib's ModelTheory, and independence is stated semantically as ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos501) ∧ ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ ∼Erdos501); a faithfulness theorem shows that in Mathlib's ZFSet the sentence is equivalent to the Mathlib statement of the first question, verbatim the proposition of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures.  All targets are proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.  As far as we know this is the first Erdős problem whose resolution is a formally verified independence result.

records.name: Certified.regts_sevenster
records.entry_name: A proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture, formalized
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture. A complex-valued graph parameter, normalized at the empty graph and invariant under isomorphism, has exponentially bounded edge-connection rank if and only if it is a mixed partition function. For a natural rank base R, a representing model can be chosen with k even and 2ℓ odd colours satisfying k + 2ℓ ≤ R. The development also proves the even connection-rank growth limit, minimum total colour dimension, minimal parity formulas and prescribed-dimension criterion. Schrijver's factorial argument supplies nilpotent-trace vanishing; semisimplicity and Deligne's fibre-functor theorem give the model; a polynomial commutant estimate gives the sharp colour budget. Deligne's theorem and the required symmetric-group character theory are proved within the development. The appendix's trace-zeta results give rationality and degree bounds, with an independent proof of nilpotent-trace vanishing. The theorems of record use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, checked by pinned audits.

records.name: TheoremA
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem A (ODE rigidity, all weights; label thm:ode, Theorem 6.1 in the current compilation of the campaign paper): if polynomials A, C over an integral domain of characteristic zero and an integer weight nu >= 1 satisfy A*C' - nu*A'*C = c for a nonzero constant c, then deg A <= 1 (TheoremA).  Also a standalone positive-characteristic strengthening extracted from the same proof (TheoremA_charP): the same conclusion over a domain of characteristic p under the degree bounds nu*deg A < p and deg C < p.  The theorem is the rigidity engine of the depth-two block analysis in the campaign on the plane Jacobian problem at Newton-degree pair (72,108).

records.name: ArithmeticOfTime.padovan_a_forces_b
records.doc: A kernel-checked chirality package for the Padovan substitution (0 ↦ 1, 1 ↦ 2, 2 ↦ 01 on Fin 3; its incidence matrix has characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1, an orientation fact that is not used or compared). Three compared theorems, all at the iterate-factor level — they quantify over factors of the concrete words S^[n] [x], never over an abstract subshift. (1) The successor invariant: in every positive iterate from any seed, the letter 0 ("a") is immediately followed by 1 ("b"). (2) Chirality: the word 20 ("ca") is a factor of an iterate while its reversal 02 ("ac") is a factor of no iterate from any seed — the factor language reads differently backwards — proved from the invariant, with no enumeration on the ac side. (3) No palindromic factor: no factor of length ≥ 4 of any iterate from any seed (including the zeroth iterate) is a palindrome, via a complete length-≤5 window certificate for the seed a together with the index shift S [0] = [1], S [1] = [2], which exhibits every seed's iterate as a seed-a iterate.

records.name: TsirelsonTightness.chsh_upper
records.doc: Kernel-checked exact-constant results for the CHSH operator T = A₀B₀ + A₀B₁ + A₁B₀ − A₁B₁ of an arbitrary CHSH tuple (Mathlib's IsCHSHTuple: self-adjoint involutions with the A's commuting with the B's). (1) The Landau identity: in any *-ring, T² = 4 + [A₀,A₁]·[B₁,B₀] — the exact, representation-independent correction to the naive T² = 8·1 (chsh_mul_self). (2) Tsirelson's bound in norm form: ‖T‖ ≤ 2√2 for every CHSH tuple in every nontrivial unital real C*-normed algebra (chsh_norm_le). (3) The classical constant, exactly: if either party's pair commutes, ‖T‖ = 2 — not merely ≤ 2 (chsh_norm_of_comm). (4) Necessity of noncommutativity: any violation ‖T‖ > 2 forces A₀A₁ ≠ A₁A₀ and B₀B₁ ≠ B₁B₀ — noncommutativity within both parties is necessary for any violation of the classical bound (noncomm_of_chsh_norm_gt_two). (5) The exact constant of M₄(ℝ): in the l2 operator norm, 2√2 is the greatest element of the set of CHSH operator norms over 4×4 real matrices — an upper bound for every tuple, attained by an explicit real-Pauli tuple (chsh_opNorm_isGreatest), so the maximal violation 2√2 is possible, not just bounded. The witness side stays compared: the explicit quadruple is verified to be a genuine CHSH tuple, its CHSH operator has eigenvalue exactly 2√2 on the explicit nonzero vector (1,0,0,1) and l2 operator norm exactly 2√2; the ordered star-ring bounds T ≤ (2√2)·1 and (commutative case) T ≤ 2 and the strict gap 2 < 2√2 complete the picture. A falsification is compared alongside: the saturating tuple's T² is not c·1 for ANY real c (chsh_sq_ne quantifies over every scalar), so the scalar-square route to the norm is closed for every scalar; the norm results here go through the C*-identity (and, for the generic bound, the Landau identity) instead.

records.name: LowRankUnivariateSOS.rankTwo_no_spurious_socp
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of Legat, Yuan and Parrilo, "Low-Rank Univariate Sum of Squares Has No Spurious Local Minima" (SIAM J. Optim. 33(3), 2023). For a real univariate polynomial p and a pair of polynomials u = (u₁, u₂), consider the quadratically penalized Burer–Monteiro objective f_p(u) = ‖σ(u) - p‖² with σ(u) = u₁² + u₂², the norm coming from any inner product on ℝ[x]. The formalized theorem states that if p is a sum of two squares (which is the case for any nonnegative  univariate polynomial) and u is a second-order critical point of f_p (vanishing gradient and positive semidefinite Hessian, Definition 3.1 of the paper), then σ(u) = p, equivalently f_p(u) = 0; hence every SOCP, and in particular every local minimum, is a global minimum. The development follows the paper's proof: the gcd decomposition u = a·u₀ with u₀ coprime, the observation that σ(u₀) has no real roots, a Bézout-based "hgroup" lemma writing a sum of squares p as g·q + s·σ(u₀) with s a sum of squares when g and σ(u₀) are coprime, the factor-peeling argument that replaces the quadratic factors of a shared with σ(u₀) by X², and the final certificate argument combining the first- and second-order conditions.

records.name: card_valid_bases
records.doc: A Lean formalization of an exact enumeration identity and two consequences: for a finite type α, the number of families B ⊆ Set α that are topological bases equals the sum, over all topologies τ on α, of 2^(|τ| − |M_τ|), where M_τ is the canonical minimal basis of minimal open neighbourhoods (Mathlib's nhdsKer {x} at each point). Kernel-reducible enumeration gives the exact table #(0)=2, #(1)=2, #(2)=10, #(3)=142. A quantitative sandwich then shows that the discrete fiber 2^(2^N − N) dominates: for N ≥ 2 the remaining fibers contribute at most 2^(N(N−1) + 3·2^(N−2)), the ratio to the discrete term tends to 1, and for N ≥ 10 the total is at most twice the discrete term. The argument is a fiber decomposition: every finite topology is Alexandrov-discrete, the minimal neighbourhoods generate it, and the bases generating τ are exactly the families B with M_τ ⊆ B ⊆ {U | τ.IsOpen U}. The informal account is the companion note CARDB.md in this repository. The Lean source was written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency.

records.name: EulerBrick.cuboid_one
records.doc: Formal proof of the First Cuboid Conjecture, which states that for all positive coprime integers a, b with a ≠ b, a certain degree-8 polynomial P_{a,b}(t) over ℤ is irreducible. This conjecture was proposed by Shapirov in "Perfect cuboids and irreducible polynomials" (arXiv:1108.5348) as part of a family of three conjectures whose combined truth would imply the nonexistence of a perfect Euler brick. The proof first analyses rational factors and the symmetry F(−x) vs F(x) to reduce irreducibility of the degree-8 polynomial to irreducibility of a degree-4 factor Q_{a,b}, and the coprime branch to a Diophantine identity. Irreducibility of Q is in turn reduced to the quartic Diophantine equation x⁴ + 34x²y² + y⁴ = z², whose only trivial solutions are established by Fermat-style infinite descent. The formal proof was autonomously discovered by the AlphaProof Nexus agent; an independent informal proof using rank-zero elliptic curves was given by Asiryan (arXiv:2510.11768).

records.name: SZ.quadPisot_notMem_S_of_two_lt
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper, which improves on a problem by Dubickas. Dubickas (Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006), 331–336) splits the reals α > 1 in two: α lies in 𝒵 when some real ξ ≠ 0 makes every integral part ⌊ξαⁿ⌋, n ≥ 1, even, and in 𝒮 otherwise. At α = 3/2 this is Mahler's question, and open; his Problem 5 asks whether 𝒮 has an element greater than 2. This formalization decides 𝒮 versus 𝒵 for every quadratic Pisot number: the golden mean is the only one in 𝒮, so none greater than 2 lies there and Problem 5 loses its whole natural class of candidates, though the problem itself stays open. The case that had resisted the source paper's four constructions is α = 1 + √2, settled by an exact computation rather than an estimate: with ξ = (2−√2)/4 one has ⌊ξ(1+√2)^(n+1)⌋ = Pₙ − [n odd] for the Pell numbers P, so every integral part is even. The mechanism generalizes: for a real quadratic pair with second conjugate in (−1,0), the closed-form multiplier ξ = −β/(α−β) makes m divide ⌊ξαⁿ⌋ for every n ≥ 0 whenever m ∣ a and m ∣ b−1 — an exact congruence, not a confinement of fractional parts — and all but finitely many of those integral parts are then composite. The informal account is the companion paper doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.20582.79689. records.name: paper_c_theorem_one_one_finite_cylinder
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of a quantitative Poisson approximation for the starting points of long constant stretches of an extended Rademacher random completely multiplicative function in a dyadic block. records.name: Erdos266.erdos_266
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization, against Mathlib, of the Kovač–Tao resolution of Erdős problem #266 (a conjecture of Stolarsky): it is not true that every sequence of positive integers with convergent reciprocal sum admits an integer shift t >= 1 making the shifted Ahmes series irrational. records.name: MPE.mpe_dithered
records.doc: Machine-checked proofs of three probabilistic convergence theorems for restarted Minimal Polynomial Extrapolation (MPE) applied to nonlinear fixed-point iterations.  Dithered restarts keep the error below the doubly exponential schedule delta^(theta^m), for any theta in (1,2), from every starting point -- the breakdown set included -- with an explicit failure-probability exponent over the dither; in the root sense the convergence order is at least theta.  Under simple spectrum, the error follows a quadratically shrinking dither schedule (root order at least 2) with failure probability linear in the initial radius up to a logarithmic factor, and MPE coincides with Reduced Rank Extrapolation at every cycle. With no dither at all, the restarted iteration from a single uniformly random starting point at worst squares the error at every cycle with high probability, under two checkable hypotheses on the Jacobian and the quadratic Taylor coefficients.  The registered statements are self-contained over mathlib: every object of the construction is introduced by an explicit defining equation among the hypotheses.

records.name: WignerReal.exists_isometry_of_transProbPreserving
records.doc:
A sequential product on the effects of an order-unit space is a binary operation a & b, read "first test a, then test b with the state updated by the first test", satisfying the seven axioms S1-S7 of van de Wetering (arXiv:1803.11139, Definition 2). This development registers two classification theorems for such products on the Hermitian matrix algebras.
On H_N(R), the Hermitian N x N real matrices with N >= 1, every sequential product is the Lueders product sqrt(a) b sqrt(a): there is no free parameter. On H_N(C) with N >= 3, every sequential product has the twist normal form a^(1/2+it) b a^(1/2-it) for a unique real t. The twist family is a one-parameter deformation of the Lueders product, and the complex theorem says nothing outside it satisfies the axioms. The equations are asserted on all effects, including singular ones, and the uniqueness of t is part of the registered statement.
Direction. Both registered classification theorems are necessity: a product satisfying the axioms is supplied, and the theorem says it has the stated normal form. The two converses differ in status and neither is registered. For the complex case, that each real t defines a SeqProd satisfying S2 is proved in the wider development; together with the registered uniqueness it is what would make the parameter map injective. For the real case, that the Lueders formula defines a SeqProd satisfying S2 is not proved anywhere in this development. Nothing here registers a bijection between parameters and products, or the admissibility of the Lueders formula.
The package also registers two classical theorems the development proves in passing. Albert's power-associativity theorem: in a commutative Jordan ring carrying an R-module structure, x^(m+1) * x^(n+1) = x^(m+n+2), with no unit, finite dimension, formal reality or positivity assumed. And the real case of Wigner's theorem: every transition probability preserving self-map of the rays of a finite-dimensional real inner product space is induced by a linear isometry, with bijectivity not assumed but derived.
Both classification theorems are proved from S1-S7 with no hypotheses beyond the dimension bounds, and their axiom closures contain only Lean's three core axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The continuity axiom S2 is stated in the order-unit norm, as an explicit epsilon-delta condition, so the statement file depends on no normed-space or topological instance; the equivalence with continuity in the carrier's Frobenius topology is proved in the development.
Scope. Comparator registers four theorems across three separate entries: the two sequential-product classifications above, which use the SeqProd interface and the axiom S2 and correspond to numbered rows of the manuscript; and the two ancillary classical theorems, Albert and Wigner, which use neither and correspond to no manuscript row. Nothing beyond those four registered theorems is claimed by this submission.
The two classification theorems are two rows of a thirty-six row manifest tracking the numbered results of the accompanying manuscript. The manuscript as a whole is not formalized: as of 2026-08-12 the manifest stands at 12 rows formalized, 19 partial, and 5 absent. In particular the quaternionic row H_n(H) and the Albert-algebra row H_3(O) of the manuscript's main theorem are not proved here, and the coalescence and diagonal-homomorphism lemmas are established on the concrete carrier H_N(C) rather than at the manuscript's stated generality of a finite-dimensional simple Euclidean Jordan algebra.

records.name: ZetaLean.Palomar.pub1_strong_closure
records.doc: A variational identity for the Fredholm operator A = I + T on the interval I = [-1/2, 1/2], where T is convolution against the Farmer-Gonek-Lee pair-correlation form factor F1(x) = |x| - 4x^2 + sum_k a_k |x|^(2k+3) with a_k = 2^(2k+3) k! / (2k+2)!. Let w = A^(-1)1 and c* = <1, A^(-1)1>. Over the source-admissible class of scalar profiles v(s) = phi(Ls)^2 induced by even, radially nonincreasing C^2 windows supported exactly on [-L/2, L/2] with 0 <= phi <= 1 and uniform L^1 bounds on phi'' and (phi^2)'', the supremum of <1,v>^2 / <Av,v> equals c*, and the infimum of the reciprocal quotient <Av,v> / <1,v>^2 equals 1/c*. The upper bound <1,v>^2 <= c* <Av,v> is energy Cauchy-Schwarz. It holds for every v, it is classical, and it is not the content of this result. The content is the reverse inequality over the constrained class: c* is the value of the unconstrained variational problem, and the identity says that imposing evenness, radial monotonicity, an exact compact support, the amplitude ceiling 0 <= phi <= 1 and uniform L^1 bounds on the second derivatives does not lower the supremum. That direction is proved by exhibiting an explicit endpoint-tapered family inside the class, indexed by the scale L, whose quotient converges to c*. Both orientations are advertised because the orientation is load-bearing: it is the quotient with <1,v>^2 in the numerator whose supremum is c*, and the supporting development also proves that the two are not interchangeable. The advertised statement is existential in the profile and in the two uniform constants, so it carries its own non-vacuity: an IsLUB or IsGLB assertion over the image of an empty class is unsatisfiable in the reals, so the theorem cannot hold unless the class is populated by the constants for which it is stated. Audience. The kernel F1 is the pair-correlation form factor and the window class is the generalized, load-bearing class of Section 7.1 of the cited paper rather than a convenient flat-topped realization, so the constrained supremum settled here is the quantity that a critical-line proportion argument built on that framework optimizes; analytic number theorists working on the proportion of zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line, and on pair correlation of its zeros, are the audience for which the exact value of that supremum over the admissible class, rather than a bound on it, is the relevant fact. The statement is also a closure result for a constrained admissible class in the variational theory of Fredholm integral operators (MSC 45B05, 49R05) and can be read there without reference to its origin. What the theorem itself asserts is bounded by the scope field below: it is a statement about a Fredholm operator on an interval and a class of test profiles, and it is evidence for nothing beyond that.
