records.name: MahlerWindow.quadratic_min
records.doc: For each degree d in {2, 3, 4}, the polynomial x^d - x - 1 attains the minimal Mahler measure among monic irreducible integer polynomials of degree d with Mahler measure above one, and the three minimal values are exactly the golden ratio (M^2 = M + 1), the plastic ratio (M^3 = M + 1), and the root of x^4 - x^3 - 1 above one (M^4 = M^3 + 1); by Siegel's classical theorem (1944, cited as background, not formalized here) the latter two are the smallest and second-smallest Pisot numbers. Classically the degree-4 minimizer is not itself a Pisot polynomial, yet its measure lands back on the Pisot list via the reciprocal transform. The minimizers' irreducibility is part of the compared surface. Proofs are by a Graeffe-certificate architecture: an effective coefficient-bound box from Mathlib's norm_coeff_le_choose_mul_mahlerMeasure, then one integer certificate per box element (tie orbit, cyclotomic cofactor, explicit factorization, or an iterated Graeffe coefficient bound), 6,171 + 147 + 21 certificates kernel-decided with plain decide — no native_decide anywhere. The exact values follow from a root-inversion identity and a (sigma, s)-reduction localizing the conjugate pairs, with multiplicity excluded by kernel-certified measure brackets.

records.name: ColorfulHelly.colorful_helly
records.doc: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Lovász's Colorful Helly Theorem (1974 / Bárány 1982). Proves that for any d + 1 finite families of convex sets in R^d such that every colorful transversal has a non-empty intersection, at least one entire family has a non-empty intersection. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.name: MeasurableSelection.exists_measurable_selection
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport, together with the descriptive-set-theoretic library it requires.  The result registered by this Comparator configuration is the Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski measurable selection theorem: for an arbitrary measurable space (alpha, A) and a Polish space Y, a multifunction Phi : alpha -> Set Y with nonempty closed values that is weakly measurable (the hit set {a | Phi a meets U} lies in A for every open U) admits an A-to-Borel measurable selection f with f a in Phi a for every a.  The statement is measure-free and pointwise: no measure appears, and the selection property holds everywhere, not almost everywhere.  It is proved from Mathlib alone, by the classical argument — a dense sequence in Y, a recursion producing measurable countably-valued approximate selectors whose successive stages stay within (1/2)^n, and a uniform Cauchy limit that is measurable as a pointwise limit of measurable functions and lands in Phi a because Phi a is closed.  The measurability of each refinement step is obtained by splitting over the countably many measurable fibres of the previous stage's index function, on each of which the test set is cut out by a fixed open set, so the weak measurability hypothesis applies directly.  No measurable selection theorem exists in Mathlib at the pinned revision.  The wider repository contains the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport in one period and over a general finite horizon, an epsilon-optimal strategy that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable at every stage and an exactly optimal Borel-measurable strategy under Feller kernels and lower semicontinuous costs (Bertsekas–Shreve 7.50 and 8.3), and the supporting descriptive set theory: Jankov–von Neumann uniformization, Choquet capacitability for analytic sets, Polishness of the space of probability measures on a Polish space, and lower semianalyticity of kernel integrals.  The measurable selection theorem is used in that development to produce plain-Borel-measurable feasible bicausal strategies.

records.name: ScottishBook155.claim14
records.doc: A Lean proof that there are real Banach spaces X and Y and a bijection U from X to Y which preserves every pairwise distance on every closed ball of radius one quarter while failing to be a global isometry. This gives a counterexample to Scottish Book Problem 155.

records.name: Capacitability.analyticSet_measure_eq_iSup_isCompact
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport, together with the descriptive-set-theoretic library it requires.  The results registered by this Comparator configuration are Choquet capacitability for analytic sets in its finite-measure form, and its immediate corollary, the universal measurability of analytic sets.  Concretely: for a Polish space X carrying its Borel sigma-algebra, a finite Borel measure mu on X, and an analytic (not necessarily Borel) set A contained in X, the outer measure of A is the supremum of mu K over the compact subsets K of A; and consequently A is null-measurable for mu, i.e. it differs from a Borel set by a mu-null set.  Both are proved from Mathlib alone.  The argument writes a nonempty analytic set as the range of a continuous map pi from Baire space, forms the Souslin scheme of closures of images of cylinders, and runs a measure-free recursion that produces, coordinate by coordinate, a bound beta with c < mu (W(beta,n)) for every n, where W(beta,n) is the closed union of the scheme pieces bounded by beta on the first n coordinates.  A subsequence extraction inside the compact set of beta-bounded branches shows that the intersection of the W(beta,n) is contained in the compact set pi '' Sigma(beta), and continuity of mu along the decreasing sequence of closed sets W(beta,n) — the one step that uses finiteness of mu — supplies the compact witness.  Universal measurability then follows by inner approximation within 1/(k+1), taking the union of the approximating compacts and comparing with a measurable hull. Neither result exists in Mathlib at the pinned revision, where inner regularity is available for measurable sets only.  The wider repository contains the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport in one period and over a general finite horizon, an epsilon-optimal strategy that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable at every stage and an exactly optimal Borel-measurable strategy under Feller kernels and lower semicontinuous costs (Bertsekas-Shreve 7.50 and 8.3), and the supporting descriptive set theory: Kuratowski-Ryll-Nardzewski measurable selection, Jankov-von Neumann uniformization, Polishness of the space of probability measures on a Polish space, and lower semianalyticity of kernel integrals.  Capacitability is what makes the last of these possible: universal measurability of analytic sets is the ingredient behind the null-measurable Fubini step in Bertsekas-Shreve 7.48.

records.name: ProbabilityMeasurePolish.polishSpace_probabilityMeasure
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport, together with the descriptive-set-theoretic library it requires.  The result registered by this Comparator configuration is the Polish-space structure of the space of probability measures: if X is a Polish space carrying its Borel sigma-algebra, then the space of Borel probability measures on X, with the topology of weak convergence, is again Polish — its topology is second countable and admits a complete compatible metric.  Mathlib at the pinned revision already supplies the Levy-Prokhorov metric, the identification of the Levy-Prokhorov topology with the topology of weak convergence on a separable space, and Prokhorov's theorem; it stops at metrizability of the space of probability measures and supplies neither completeness nor separability.  Both are proved here.  Completeness: a Levy-Prokhorov Cauchy sequence is uniformly tight, the compact witness being an intersection over j of finite unions of closed balls of radius 2^(-j), whose heads are covered using a countable dense sequence and continuity from below and whose tails are transferred between members of the sequence along the Levy-Prokhorov inequality; Prokhorov's theorem then produces a convergent subsequence, and a Cauchy sequence with a convergent subsequence converges.  Separability: normalized natural-weight mixtures of Dirac measures at points of a countable dense sequence are dense in Levy-Prokhorov distance.  Complete plus separable metric gives a Polish structure on the Levy-Prokhorov space, which Mathlib's homeomorphism LevyProkhorov.probabilityMeasureHomeomorph transports to the space of probability measures with the weak topology.  The wider repository contains the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport in one period and over a general finite horizon, an epsilon-optimal strategy that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable at every stage and an exactly optimal Borel-measurable strategy under Feller kernels and lower semicontinuous costs (Bertsekas-Shreve 7.50 and 8.3), and the supporting descriptive set theory: Jankov-von Neumann uniformization, the Kuratowski-Ryll-Nardzewski measurable selection theorem, Choquet capacitability for analytic sets, and lower semianalyticity of kernel integrals.  The registered result is used in that development to make the space of probability measures a legitimate Polish parameter space for kernels and for the Bellman recursion.

records.name: Uniformization.jankov_von_neumann
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport, together with the descriptive-set-theoretic library it requires.  The result registered by this Comparator configuration is the Jankov-von Neumann uniformization theorem: for Polish spaces X and Y and a nonempty analytic (Sigma-1-1) set P in X x Y, there is a function phi : X -> Y that uniformizes P on its projection, (x, phi x) in P for every x in proj_X(P), and that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable, meaning that phi-preimages of Borel subsets of Y lie in the sigma-algebra generated by the analytic subsets of X.  The statement of record writes both sigma-algebras out in full, so it mentions only Mathlib notions and no bespoke definition: the domain sigma-algebra is MeasurableSpace.generateFrom {s | MeasureTheory.AnalyticSet s} (Bertsekas-Shreve Definition 7.19) and the codomain sigma-algebra is borel Y, given explicitly rather than through an ambient instance.  The proof is Kechris's own argument for 18.1: write the analytic P as the range of a continuous map from Baire space, pull it back to a closed set F in X x (N -> N), uniformize F by the leftmost branch of the section tree, and push forward.  The measurability of the leftmost branch is proved cylinder by cylinder: the preimage of a basic cylinder is a countable Boolean combination of projections of closed sets, hence lies in sigma(Sigma-1-1). Unlike the textbook proof, the Lean development never reduces the domain to Baire space, so the invariance of sigma(Sigma-1-1) under Borel isomorphism is never needed. Neither the theorem nor the analytic sigma-algebra exists in Mathlib at the pinned revision.  The wider repository contains the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport in one period and over a general finite horizon, an epsilon-optimal strategy that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable at every stage and an exactly optimal Borel-measurable strategy under Feller kernels and lower semicontinuous costs (Bertsekas-Shreve 7.50 and 8.3), and the supporting descriptive set theory: Kuratowski-Ryll-Nardzewski measurable selection, Choquet capacitability for analytic sets, Polishness of the space of probability measures on a Polish space, and lower semianalyticity of kernel integrals.  Jankov-von Neumann is the selection engine of that development: it is what produces the sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable epsilon-optimal strategies.

records.name: Challenge.gaussianFreeField_satisfies_OS_axioms
records.doc: Construction of the massive Gaussian Free Field in Euclidean spacetime of any dimension d >= 2 as a probability measure on the tempered distributions S'(R^d), and a proof that it satisfies all of the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms: OS0 analyticity, OS1 regularity, OS2 Euclidean invariance, OS3 reflection positivity, and OS4 clustering and ergodicity. The OS axioms are the conditions under which a Euclidean field theory reconstructs a relativistic quantum field theory obeying the Wightman axioms, so the free field is the base case of constructive quantum field theory on which interacting constructions are built. The development is dimension-generic: one proof parameterized by d, consuming the free covariance only through a typeclass whose per-dimension input is a single closed-form radial kernel identified with the proper-time integral, with concrete instances at d = 2, 3, 4, 5. The result addresses three research audiences. In constructive quantum field theory, the free field satisfying OS0-OS4 is the base case (Glimm-Jaffe, ch. 6) on which interacting constructions such as P(phi)_2 and phi^4_3 are built, so a machine-checked base case is the reusable starting point for any formalized interacting construction. The analytic chain is proved rather than assumed: the Minlos theorem and the Hilbert-nuclearity of Schwartz space are consumed from the bochner and gaussian-field developments as theorems, nuclearity in the general form for Schwartz functions on any finite-dimensional real normed space, so every headline result depends on nothing beyond Lean's three foundational axioms. In stochastic quantization and singular SPDEs, the massive GFF constructed here is the reference Gaussian and the invariant measure of the free dynamics in every dimension treated. And for researchers formalizing quantum field theory in various dimensions, this is, to our knowledge, the first machine-checked verification of the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms — the literature search supporting that statement (scope, terms, dates, and the related-but-distinct work found) is documented in docs/novelty.md of this repository — with the dimension-generic propagator typeclass as the designed extension point for further covariances and dimensions.

records.name: BB61.QuadSetup.equidistributed_iff_exists_invariant_measure
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of criteria for Bugeaud's Problem 10.61 ([Bug12, p. 222], due to Mendès France [MF67]): for a Pisot number α > 2 and the Cantor set C(α) = {(α−1) Σ_{k≥1} ε_k α^{−k} : ε_k ∈ {0,1}}, no ξ ∈ C(α) has (ξαⁿ)_{n≥1} uniformly distributed modulo one. The problem is open; what is proved here are criteria for it and two instances. Every compared statement that concludes Problem 10.61 does so for a *quadratic* setup — a real root α > 1 of X² − aX − b whose conjugate has modulus below one — and the two instances are quadratic; the arbitrary-degree material is conditional ingredients, from which no compared statement derives non-equidistribution. Seventeen statements are compared, in four groups. (A) The reduction to symbolic dynamics is an equivalence, and it is complete. (i) Some ξ ∈ C(α) is u.d. mod 1 iff the full two-shift {0,1}^ℤ carries a shift-invariant Borel probability measure whose push-forward under an explicit factor map F is Lebesgue measure on 𝕋. (ii) 10.61 holds at α iff a finite certificate witnesses it: a mean-zero real trigonometric polynomial G on 𝕋 and a c > 0 with ∫ G∘F dμ ≥ c for every invariant μ. (iii) The pressure bracket that makes such a search terminate, −c/β ≤ ∫ g dμ over every invariant μ whenever the pressure of −βg relative to a finite partition is at most c. (B) A pressure criterion. (ii) A bounded measurable potential annihilated by every counterexample measure, an entropy floor h_min for those measures, and a partition pressure below h_min together prove 10.61 at α; and its machine form, where the potential carries a finite-state transfer bound with an integer vector certificate, the hypothesis comparing the log of the certificate ratio, less the Lebesgue mean, against h_min. (iv) The budget identity A(α)·h_min(α) = log 2, tying the Route A exponent to the floor. (C) A covering criterion for quadratic setups, and arbitrary-degree ingredients. (i) Two real inequalities — the depth slope 1 + L/R − L is negative exactly when (L−1)(R−1) > 1, and at the balanced depth M′ = ⌈M·L/R⌉ the covering total obeys an explicit logarithmic bound linear in M with that slope — and then, for a quadratic setup, a numeric certificate at depths (M, M′) yielding one open interval J ⊆ (0,1), uniform in ξ and in n, that every orbit misses at every time, whence A(α) < 1 implies 10.61 at α. (ii) For a quadratic setup of norm −b, the criterion applies exactly when (log₂ α − 1)(log₂(α/|b|) − 1) > 1. This characterizes when A(α) < 1; it does not decide Problem 10.61 for quadratic α with A(α) ≥ 1, about which nothing is compared. (iii) Three ingredients about the family Xᵈ − aXᵈ⁻¹ − 1, valid at every degree d ≥ 2: for a ≥ 3 the real root exceeding a is a Pisot number; every other conjugate has modulus at most (2/a)^{1/(d−1)}; and the numerical inequality log 2/log α + log 2/log(1/ρ) < 1 holds whenever a ≥ 2^{d+1}, a < α, ρ > 0 and a·ρᵈ⁻¹ ≤ 2. These are ingredients, not a criterion: no compared statement carries them to Problem 10.61 above degree two, because (i) is proved only for quadratic setups. At degree two the family members are quadratic setups, and the first of them is α = 2+√5. (D) The two numbers at which the machinery is run to a conclusion, both quadratic: at α = 2+√5 the strong form — an explicit interval missed by every orbit at every time — and 10.61 itself; and at α = 2+√3, 10.61 by a confinement-gap certificate. The informal account is the repository's paper.pdf: machine-written notes documenting the Lean development, not a prior paper that the development formalizes. Credit in contributor terms rather than bibliographic ones: the mathematics and the Lean text are the agents' work, the Fable-5 agent having written the notes and the Opus-5 agent the formalization, each directed turn by turn by Ralf Stephan, who chose the targets, selected which outputs to keep, and releases the files. He does not endorse the informal arguments and has not independently verified informal-to-formal fidelity; where the prose disagrees with the challenge file, the challenge file wins. Every compared statement depends on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and nothing else.

records.name: BuschTheorem.homogeneity_automatic
records.doc: Kernel-checked proof of Busch's theorem in finite dimension: every generalized probability measure on the effects of a complex matrix algebra — nonnegative on effects, additive whenever a sum of effects is again an effect, normalized at the identity — is represented by a unique density matrix via the trace pairing. Existence and uniqueness are both compared (busch_representation). The result is the uniqueness of the Born rule in the POVM reading; it is valid in every finite dimension (beyond finiteness and decidable equality of the index type, the compared statement assumes only [Nonempty n]) and holds already at dimension 2, where Gleason's theorem (which requires dimension at least 3) does not apply. No continuity is assumed: for a normalized measure, nonnegativity plus additivity force real homogeneity on the effect interval (scalars in [0,1]), compared separately as homogeneity_automatic. The compared statements use only Mathlib vocabulary (Matrix.PosSemidef, Matrix.trace).

records.name: Superorthogonal.sqfct_estimate_of_type_iv_superorthogonal
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the main result (Theorem 1) of the paper  "A new type of superorthogonality" by P. T. Gressman, L. B. Pierce, J. Roos, and P.-L. Yung; arXiv:2212.08956, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 152, 665-675, 2024. The theorem provides a simple criterion on a family of functions that implies a square function estimate on Lp for every even integer p ≥ 2. This defines a new type of superorthogonality that is verified by checking a less restrictive criterion than any other type of superorthogonality previously known.

records.name: GraphCoveringTheory.KuroshChallenge.kurosh_bass_serre_decomposition_challenge
records.doc: Formalizes the sharp Schreier index formula for finite-index subgroups of free groups and the Kurosh subgroup theorem for arbitrary subgroups of indexed free products. The Schreier proof realizes a subgroup as the vertex group of a finite action-groupoid covering, while the Kurosh proof constructs the Bass--Serre tree, a locally bijective graph-of-groups cover, and its path-lifting normal form. The Kurosh factor-only statement is a free product of the nontrivial quotient vertex stabilizers and the free group of the quotient graph; each vertex stabilizer is identified with an intersection with a conjugate of an original factor. For finite-index normal subgroups, a companion module proves that every deck transformation of the finite Schreier action is a unique right translation by the quotient group.

records.name: DilworthTheorem.dilworth_theorem
records.doc: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Dilworth's Theorem (Robert P. Dilworth, 1950) on chain decompositions of finite posets and Mirsky's Dual Theorem (Leon Mirsky, 1971) on antichain covers. Proves that the maximum size of an antichain equals the minimum number of chains covering the poset, and dually that the maximum length of a chain equals the minimum number of antichains covering the poset. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.doc: Malliavin calculus on abstract Gaussian Banach spaces, formalized in Lean 4 against Mathlib. records.name: MarshallHall.marshallHall
records.entry_name: Marshall Hall's theorem through finite cores
records.doc: Formalizes Marshall Hall's finite-index free-factor theorem for finitely generated subgroups of finite-rank free groups. The proof extracts the finitely many suffix states of a subgroup generating set, completes the resulting partial generator actions to permutations of a finite state set, identifies the connected orbit with a finite core, and extends a geodesic spanning tree to obtain an inclusion-compatible free-product decomposition. The repository also proves binary and finite-indexed free-group instances of Grushko--Neumann rank additivity, the arbitrary-factor binary theorem, and the LERF consequence. The arbitrary-factor proof is carried by a finite labelled-graph fold, source-unfold, and monochromatic-vertex contraction reduction.

records.name: FriendshipWindmill.friendship_windmill
records.doc: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Friendship Windmill Structure Theorem (Erdős, Rényi, and Sós, 1966). Proves that any finite graph in which every pair of distinct vertices shares exactly one common neighbor possesses a universal vertex w, has an odd number of vertices |V| = 2k + 1, induces a 1-regular perfect matching on V \ {w}, and is isomorphic to the Dutch windmill graph Wd(k, 2) To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.name: Headline.schurMod_eq
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of modular Schur numbers. For m ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2, put n = m/gcd(m,ℓ-1). The main result proves the uniform closed form S_m(k,ℓ) = n-1 for every k ≥ n-1. The development also proves the integer-to-residue formulation and lossless N ≤ m-1 bound, singleton-safety and zero-class obstructions, the exact one-color formula for 2 ≤ ℓ ≤ m, and the stated sigma-infinity coset-cardinality bound. Mathlib-only Headline statements are checked by the Palomar Comparator configuration. A separate public 27-module hand-written, generated-independent project layer contains named canonical-cover seed count, stable-prime transport and recurrence, prime-power, and unrestricted exponent-truncation capstones; those capstones have a separate transitive-axiom audit and are outside the Comparator's statement-comparison gate. The earlier generated native_decide scan tree is excluded from the public release and verification claims.

records.name: EntangledBorn.separable_chsh_le
records.entry_name: The entangled Born correlations: a mixed-state entanglement witness through the Born rule forced on the composite algebra
records.doc: Kernel-checked entanglement package on the bipartite matrix algebra (2x2 tensor 2x2, native product index): (1) the separable-state CHSH bound 2 for the real-Pauli tuple, proved through the Bloch-disk constraint with no spectral theory; (2) an entanglement witness — a bipartite state, positive semidefinite with unit trace, that is NOT separable, with Born CHSH expectation equal to the Tsirelson value 2*sqrt(2) (the Bell state, exhibited explicitly in the Solution); (3) spectral projections without spectral theory — (1+W)/2 is an effect for every Hermitian involution W, any finite dimension; (4) the two-party correlation law forced, not postulated: for any state representing a generalized probability measure on effects (Busch's theorem vocabulary; no continuity assumed), the correlation at any pair of binary-observable settings is an explicit difference of the measure's values at two effects; (5) the assembly — a state that is not separable, is the UNIQUE state reproducing its own effect statistics (Born-rule uniqueness on the composite algebra), attains the Tsirelson value, and carries the witness correlation table XX = ZZ = 1, XZ = ZX = 0. Extended (second session, 2026-08-31) by five further compared theorems — the general bounds and the quantitative Werner-family layer: (6) the separable bound 2 at ARBITRARY finite local dimensions and arbitrary Hermitian-involution settings; (7) the state-level Tsirelson bound 2*sqrt(2) at the same generality; (8) the Werner family W_p = p|Phi+><Phi+| + ((1-p)/4)1, spelled inline from the explicit Bell projector, has CHSH expectation at most 2*sqrt(2)*p at any Hermitian-involution settings with traceless party-1 observables (p >= 0) — the Werner line of the Horodecki 1995 criterion; (9) the violation threshold: for p >= 0, W_p violates CHSH at some such settings iff p > 1/sqrt(2); (10) the separability endpoint (Werner 1989): W_p is separable for 0 <= p <= 1/3. All hypotheses are inline; the compared statements use only Mathlib vocabulary (Matrix.PosSemidef, Matrix.IsHermitian, Matrix.trace, the Kronecker product, Real.sqrt, Matrix.vecMulVec) with no custom definitions.

records.doc: Kernel-checked entanglement package on the bipartite matrix algebra (2x2 tensor 2x2, native product index): (1) the separable-state CHSH bound 2 for the real-Pauli tuple, proved through the Bloch-disk constraint with no spectral theory; (2) an entanglement witness — a bipartite state, positive semidefinite with unit trace, that is NOT separable, with Born CHSH expectation equal to the Tsirelson value 2*sqrt(2) (the Bell state, exhibited explicitly in the Solution); (3) spectral projections without spectral theory — (1+W)/2 is an effect for every Hermitian involution W, any finite dimension; (4) the two-party correlation law forced, not postulated: for any state representing a generalized probability measure on effects (Busch's theorem vocabulary; no continuity assumed), the correlation at any pair of binary-observable settings is an explicit difference of the measure's values at two effects; (5) the assembly — a state that is not separable, is the UNIQUE state reproducing its own effect statistics (Born-rule uniqueness on the composite algebra), attains the Tsirelson value, and carries the witness correlation table XX = ZZ = 1, XZ = ZX = 0. Extended (second session, 2026-08-31) by five further compared theorems — the general bounds and the quantitative Werner-family layer: (6) the separable bound 2 at ARBITRARY finite local dimensions and arbitrary Hermitian-involution settings; (7) the state-level Tsirelson bound 2*sqrt(2) at the same generality; (8) the Werner family W_p = p|Phi+><Phi+| + ((1-p)/4)1, spelled inline from the explicit Bell projector, has CHSH expectation at most 2*sqrt(2)*p at any Hermitian-involution settings with traceless party-1 observables (p >= 0) — the Werner line of the Horodecki 1995 criterion; (9) the violation threshold: for p >= 0, W_p violates CHSH at some such settings iff p > 1/sqrt(2); (10) the separability endpoint (Werner 1989): W_p is separable for 0 <= p <= 1/3. All hypotheses are inline; the compared statements use only Mathlib vocabulary (Matrix.PosSemidef, Matrix.IsHermitian, Matrix.trace, the Kronecker product, Real.sqrt, Matrix.vecMulVec) with no custom definitions.

records.name: PalomarSpectralStone.spectral_theorem_intrinsic
records.doc: The spectral theorem for possibly unbounded self-adjoint operators on complex Hilbert spaces, formalized through the Cayley transform and real projection-valued measures. The selected spectral theorem constructs a PVM whose scalar measures give the exact finite-second-moment domain and first-moment quadratic form, with measurable-set uniqueness, and is proved equivalent to equality with the unbounded coordinate spectral integral. The selected Stone theorem proves both that strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups have self-adjoint generators and that every self-adjoint operator generates such a group.

records.name: PlasticThreshold.plastic_salem_family
records.entry_name: The compositum of the two Mahler minimizers: exact measure, conjugate census, house, and minimal product recurrence, with the Bedford-Kim plastic family and Lehmer's polynomial
records.doc: Kernel-checked certificates for the multiplicative compositum of the two registered Mahler minimizers — rho, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 (the plastic number: Smyth's nonreciprocal minimum, Siegel's smallest Pisot number) and Q, the real root > 1 of x^4 = x + 1 (the degree-4 entry of the minimal-measure tables) — together with the Bedford-Kim spectral family whose limit rho is. Seventeen compared theorems. The spectral half: (1) for n >= 7 the family chi_n(x) = x^(n+1)(x^3 - x - 1) + (x^3 + x^2 - 1) has a canonical root in [117/100, rho), largest below rho, strictly increasing, tending to rho; (2) every chi_n is strictly positive on [rho, infinity); (3) chi_7 = (x - 1) * L exactly, over any commutative ring, with L Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial; (4) L has a root in [117/100, rho). The compositum half, for the degree-12 minimal polynomial of rho * Q (written out in full in every compared statement): (5) an exclusion witness — a nonreal quartic root z with 1 < |rho * z| < rho * Q; (6) the twelve embedding products ARE the conjugates of rho * Q, both directions; (7) there are exactly twelve of them; (8) rho * Q is an algebraic unit, via an explicit degree-11 cofactor over any commutative ring — the (3, 4, 12) triple in the normal form alpha * beta * gamma = 1; (9) the degree-12 polynomial is not reciprocal (neither its reversal nor the reversal's negation), placing it in the regime of Smyth's theorem; (10) degree multiplicativity — deg minpoly(rho*Q) = deg minpoly(rho) * deg minpoly(Q) = 12; (11) the compositum in sup form Q(rho) join Q(Q) = Q(rho*Q), of degree 12, with the two simple extensions linearly disjoint; (12) the complete unit-circle census — EXACTLY 5 conjugates strictly outside, EXACTLY 7 strictly inside, NONE on the circle, so rho * Q is neither a Pisot nor a Salem number; (13) the house — every conjugate other than rho * Q has modulus strictly below rho * Q; (14) the exact Mahler measure M = rho^2 * Q^2 * psi, where psi is the real root > 1 of psi^4 = psi^3 + 1; (15) the registry bridge — M(X^4 - X - 1) = psi and M(rulerPoly) = (rho * Q)^2 * M(X^4 - X - 1), re-proving in-repo the quantity pinned in registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004; (16) the order-12 Hadamard product recurrence — the termwise product of any solutions of the cubic and quartic shift recurrences satisfies the order-12 recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is exactly the degree-12 polynomial, in any Q-algebra; (17) the annihilator ideal of the product power sequence n |-> (rho * Q)^n is EXACTLY the principal ideal of the degree-12 polynomial — the classical order <= 3 * 4 bound is an equality, forced by the polynomial's kernel-held irreducibility. The results address three research audiences: the degree problem for products and composita of algebraic numbers (the certified (3,4,12) witness at a canonically distinguished pair, in the field's own unit-product normal form); the Mahler-measure tradition (the measure of the composed product of the two degree-minimal polynomials, in closed form in the second-smallest Pisot number); and composed products of polynomials (a certified rational instance where the finite-field coprimality criterion is unavailable and irreducibility is proved by elimination) — with the Lean audience served by concrete exercise of the Mahler-measure and linear-disjointness APIs. Like the golden ratio, rho * Q is an algebraic unit of norm -1; the compared cofactor identity is that norm computation, certified. No novelty claim is made for the measure identity (the entry is not aware of it in the literature; the claimed contribution is the kernel certificate), no "first formalization" claim is made anywhere, and whether rho is ATTAINED as a dynamical degree is open in the literature — no statement claims it. Hypotheses are inline: rho, Q, psi enter only through their defining equations plus root-selection inequalities, and the compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary (Filter.Tendsto, nhds, the complex norm, minpoly, Polynomial.rootSet, Set.ncard, Polynomial.mahlerMeasure, IntermediateField adjoin/sup, Module.finrank, Finset.range sums) — zero custom definitions. The name prefix "ruler" in statement names is the source project's term for the product rho * Q; nothing in any statement depends on it.

records.name: HadamardBFormal.theoremA
records.entry_name: hadamard-b-formal: the bordered Goethals-Seidel characterisation, the s=1 layer, and Theorem D
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of part of the theorem layer of the Hadamard-B note on bordered Goethals-Seidel arrays: twenty-six compared theorems over fifty-eight compared definitions. Theorem A characterises, by an if-and-only-if, when a Goethals-Seidel array of four sign-valued sequences over a finite abelian group extends to a Hadamard matrix through a border of width 4s whose strips are constant on the cosets of a subgroup. Theorem B is its house form, whose hypothesis is exactly a two-tier periodic-autocorrelation profile, and carries two classical degenerations at an arbitrary reflection shift: the Goethals-Seidel theorem over an arbitrary finite abelian group, and the Wallis-Whiteman/Spence bordered construction. Of Theorem C only the row-sum rows D5 and D6 are formalized; clauses D1-D4 and the classification corollary are not. The character-twist layer is Lemma T, the s = 1 profile bijection, and the theorem that a twist fixing the reflection shift is a diagonal conjugation. Theorem D is covered at clauses (D-a) through (D-e): the forced Gram and border tables, the collapse of (H4) to a single 4x4 equation, the integer Parseval identity, both directions of the transport across the doubling, and clause (D-a'), which identifies the degenerate branch with the index-one construction entry for entry, again in both directions. The index-two collapse corollary is represented by its seed-problem bijection clause alone; its characteristic-subgroup and equivariance clauses are not formalized, nor is the 768-squared census behind (D-e). Two witness records are imported under SHA-256 pins, cross-checked against the source's canonical matrix digests, and checked by kernel reduction against Theorem A's hypotheses, giving Hadamard matrices of orders 52 and 20 through the theorem rather than by matrix multiplication; no novelty of existence is claimed at either order.

records.name: MorphicNumbers.morphic_iff
records.entry_name: Only two morphic numbers: the Aarts-Fokkink-Kruijtzer classification of the golden ratio and the plastic number
records.doc: Kernel-checked classification of the morphic numbers — the reals p > 1 satisfying both of the golden ratio's defining scale closures: p + 1 = p^k (the sum of consecutive measures of the geometric system is again a measure) and p - 1 = p^(-l) (so is their difference; rendered zpow-free as p^l * (p - 1) = 1). These two equations are the arithmetic of self-similar proportion: a number satisfying both generates a measure system closed under the paper's superposition and juxtaposition, the property pair behind the divine proportion's standing as the plane's design constant. The theorem (Aarts-Fokkink-Kruijtzer 2001): there exist only two such numbers — the golden ratio, with (k, l) = (2, 1), and the plastic number, the real root of x^3 = x + 1, with (k, l) = (3, 4). Four compared statements carry the classification in full: existence of the cubic's root, the iff pinning every morphic number to the golden ratio or that root, and the two witnesses. The list of numbers with the golden ratio's defining property pair is thereby provably complete at two. The second member is a distinguished constant independently of this theorem: the plastic number is the smallest Pisot number (Siegel 1944); its minimal polynomial x^3 - x - 1 attains the minimal Mahler measure among monic irreducible integer cubics (kernel-certified in the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004), and by Smyth's theorem its measure — the number itself — is the global minimum of the Mahler measure over nonreciprocal integer polynomials; it is the growth rate of the Padovan and Perrin sequences, the cubic analogue of Fibonacci growth; and it is the threshold constant of the Blanc-Cantat classification of birational surface dynamical degrees, the spectral limit of the Bedford-Kim automorphism family (kernel-certified in the author's mahler-minimizer-compositum entry). It entered mathematics from architecture: Dom Hans van der Laan introduced it (Le Nombre Plastique, 1960) as the ideal ratio of three-dimensional proportion — the same discovery made independently by Cordonnier — and Kruijtzer conjectured, and Aarts-Fokkink-Kruijtzer proved, that van der Laan's number is the only companion the golden ratio has. What "morphic" adds to the plastic number's distinctions is finality: the golden ratio's arithmetic of self-similarity, taken as a definition, has exactly one more solution among the reals. The formalized proof consumes Selmer's trinomial irreducibility theorem from Mathlib, derives the needed Tverberg-type instance through a mirror-dichotomy argument carried out entirely in the integer polynomial ring (simplifying the paper's complex-root analysis; disclosed in the fidelity block), and closes with the factorization endgame forcing (n, m) = (3, 5). No formalization of the morphic classification, the plastic number, or the Padovan/Perrin constants exists in any surveyed prover as of the 2026-09-01 sweep; Mathlib's golden-ratio development supplies one witness's vocabulary. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

records.doc: Kernel-checked classification of the morphic numbers — the reals p > 1 satisfying both of the golden ratio's defining scale closures: p + 1 = p^k (the sum of consecutive measures of the geometric system is again a measure) and p - 1 = p^(-l) (so is their difference; rendered zpow-free as p^l * (p - 1) = 1). These two equations are the arithmetic of self-similar proportion: a number satisfying both generates a measure system closed under the paper's superposition and juxtaposition, the property pair behind the divine proportion's standing as the plane's design constant. The theorem (Aarts-Fokkink-Kruijtzer 2001): there exist only two such numbers — the golden ratio, with (k, l) = (2, 1), and the plastic number, the real root of x^3 = x + 1, with (k, l) = (3, 4). Four compared statements carry the classification in full: existence of the cubic's root, the iff pinning every morphic number to the golden ratio or that root, and the two witnesses. The list of numbers with the golden ratio's defining property pair is thereby provably complete at two. The second member is a distinguished constant independently of this theorem: the plastic number is the smallest Pisot number (Siegel 1944); its minimal polynomial x^3 - x - 1 attains the minimal Mahler measure among monic irreducible integer cubics (kernel-certified in the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004), and by Smyth's theorem its measure — the number itself — is the global minimum of the Mahler measure over nonreciprocal integer polynomials; it is the growth rate of the Padovan and Perrin sequences, the cubic analogue of Fibonacci growth; and it is the threshold constant of the Blanc-Cantat classification of birational surface dynamical degrees, the spectral limit of the Bedford-Kim automorphism family (kernel-certified in the author's mahler-minimizer-compositum entry). It entered mathematics from architecture: Dom Hans van der Laan introduced it (Le Nombre Plastique, 1960) as the ideal ratio of three-dimensional proportion — the same discovery made independently by Cordonnier — and Kruijtzer conjectured, and Aarts-Fokkink-Kruijtzer proved, that van der Laan's number is the only companion the golden ratio has. What "morphic" adds to the plastic number's distinctions is finality: the golden ratio's arithmetic of self-similarity, taken as a definition, has exactly one more solution among the reals. The formalized proof consumes Selmer's trinomial irreducibility theorem from Mathlib, derives the needed Tverberg-type instance through a mirror-dichotomy argument carried out entirely in the integer polynomial ring (simplifying the paper's complex-root analysis; disclosed in the fidelity block), and closes with the factorization endgame forcing (n, m) = (3, 5). No formalization of the morphic classification, the plastic number, or the Padovan/Perrin constants exists in any surveyed prover as of the 2026-09-01 sweep; Mathlib's golden-ratio development supplies one witness's vocabulary. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

records.name: HowsonChallenge.howson_intersection_fg
records.entry_name: Howson's theorem through finite cores and Kurosh decomposition
records.doc: Formalizes Howson's theorem for finite-rank free groups: the intersection of two finitely generated subgroups is finitely generated. The proof uses the repository's inclusion-compatible Marshall Hall construction to place one subgroup as a free factor of a finite-index overgroup, applies Schreier's finite-index theorem to the other subgroup, and then uses the actual Kurosh decomposition of the resulting subgroup of a binary free product. The final map from the relevant conjugate-intersection factor is defined from the factor inclusions and proved surjective onto the internal subgroup intersection.

records.name: Metatheory.Palomar433.checked_complete_confluence
records.doc: A Lean 4.33.0 formalization of a generic soundness theorem for finite, proof-carrying decreasing-diagram certificates. An artifact lists the labeled rewrite steps and explicit decreasing valleys for every local peak; an executable checker validates the finite data, while a separate completeness proof connects that data to the semantic relation. The theorem assumes `WellFounded lt` for the label order and then derives confluence of the unlabeled relation even though the underlying rewrite relation itself need not terminate. The repository includes a nontrivial funnel regression with three local peaks and negative certificate tests, plus a generated family study of canonical compression.

records.name: BooleanFun.BV.dictator_of_condorcet_and_unanimous
records.doc: This is a formalization in Lean 4 of Arrow's theorem for three-candidate elections as stated in Ryan O'Donnell's book "Analysis of Boolean Functions", Sec. 2.5, with a single voting rule applied to every pairwise election. The theorem states that every unanimous voting rule that always admits a Condorcet winner  must be a dictatorship, i.e. there must exist a voter that alone determines the outcome. Here voting rules are encoded by Boolean-valued functions on the Hamming cube. The proof follows the exposition given there, which is based on Gil Kalai's Fourier-analytic argument using the Walsh-Fourier transform. The version stated in the book  and formalized here is not the most general version of Arrow's theorem: for example, one may allow more than three candidates, or that the voting rules for each pairwise election are different. This formalization was entirely human-written.

records.name: FamilyBoundary.family_root_exists_unique
records.entry_name: The golden family's boundary at n = 3: general-n theorems for x^n = x + 1
records.doc: Kernel-checked general-n theorems for the golden family — the ladder of trinomials x^n - x - 1, whose unique real root r_n > 1 descends from the golden ratio (n = 2) through the plastic number (n = 3) toward 1. The family's structural boundary falls at n = 3; this entry proves the morphic half unconditionally at general n and holds the Pisot half as the measure⟺Pisot equivalence, the unconditional n = 4 non-Pisot statement, and the Siegel-conditional strict excess for n >= 4, from the family's own arithmetic, with no per-degree case check above the boundary. Eleven compared statements carry the surface. (1) The root ladder: for every n >= 2 the root exists, is unique above 1, and strictly decreases in n. (2) The morphic boundary, UNCONDITIONAL: r_n satisfies the golden ratio's two scale closures p + 1 = p^k and p - 1 = p^(-l) (Aarts-Fokkink-Kruijtzer 2001, spelled inline) if and only if n <= 3 — the classification pins morphic numbers to the golden ratio and the plastic number, and descent puts r_n below 1.23, hence below both, for n >= 4. (3) Circle exclusion: x^n - x - 1 has no complex root of modulus 1, for any n (|z| = |z + 1| = 1 forces z^2 + z + 1 = 0, so z^3 = 1, and every residue of n mod 3 is impossible). (4) The Jensen lower bound r_n <= M(x^n - x - 1), by the monic root-product form of the Mahler measure. (5) The equivalence M(x^n - x - 1) = r_n iff every other complex root lies strictly inside the unit circle — the honest form of "the family's Mahler-measure boundary IS its Pisot boundary": the equivalence is itself the kernel theorem (exact because the family never has unimodular roots, and its trinomials are separable by Selmer irreducibility), stated once and never counted as a pair of separate boundaries. (6) The Siegel-conditional closure: IF the plastic number is the smallest Pisot number — Siegel 1944, entering ONLY as an explicit named hypothesis, with "Pisot" unfolded in the statement — THEN r_n < M(x^n - x - 1) for every n >= 4. Siegel's minimality is the single classical input anywhere in the entry; every other statement is kernel-checked unconditionally, and Siegel's theorem itself is not proved here. (7) Q < psi: the quartic root (q^4 = q + 1) lies strictly below psi (psi^4 = psi^3 + 1), the Mahler measure of the n = 4 member. (8) THE SHARED LEMMA, at general n: no root of x^n - x - 1 satisfies z^2 + z + 1 = 0 (z^3 = 1 and every residue of n mod 3 is impossible). It supplies the obstruction in the circle exclusion (3), which is re-derived from it as an explicit corollary (the circle geometry supplies the reduction), and up to the substitution z^n = z + 1 (under which z^n + z^2 = 0 iff z^2 + z + 1 = 0) it is Mathlib's public Polynomial.X_pow_sub_X_sub_one_irreducible_aux — the first step of Mathlib's Selmer proof, hence of the morphic classification behind (2) — restated in the family's own vocabulary; compared as the named shared core, not as new mathematics. (9) Witness b_3 (b^3 = b^2 + 1): every other complex root of x^3 = x^2 + 1 has modulus < 1, and b_3 is not morphic. (10) Witness psi (psi^4 = psi^3 + 1): every other complex root of x^4 = x^3 + 1 has modulus < 1, and psi is not morphic. (11) The golden quartic root is NOT Pisot: for q^4 = q + 1, some complex root of x^4 = x + 1 other than q has modulus > 1 (every nonreal root does — quartic_conj_norm_gt_one in the proof module, not compared) — with (10) and (7) the degree-4 separation: Q and psi are both algebraic units with constant term of modulus one (unit-ness is elementary and not compared: Q^-1 = Q^3 - 1, psi^-1 = psi^3 - psi^2), yet Q is not Pisot and psi is, so the unit condition alone does not locate the Pisot boundary. (10) and (11) are not independent evidence: x^4 - x^3 - 1 is the image of x^4 - x - 1 under x -> -1/x, so the Pisot half of (10) says x^4 - x - 1 has one root inside the unit circle and three outside, and (11) follows; they are compared separately for the two families' sakes. THE STORY: one shared lemma beneath both boundaries (naming the family-specific arithmetic core, not the whole proof graph: (2) and (6) also share the elementary descent r_n < 1.23 < rho, and the kernel-held Pisot side is localized by Siegel plus descent, the angle route being context); the boundaries localize by different routes — an angle for Pisot (the escape arc between the primitive cube roots of unity, giving the outside-root count 1 + 2*floor((2n - 1)/6), Howell-Kyle 2018 Theorem 3 via the reciprocal trinomial; context, NOT formalized), a degree for morphic (the cofactor x^2 - x + 1 forcing k = 3; formalized) — and the classes are in fact separable: (9)-(11) hold the witnesses and the degree-4 separation in the kernel, with no Siegel input, showing the classes coming apart inside the sister trinomial family itself (Pisot units below phi that are not morphic). The entry never claims the two boundaries are independent (they share the lemma) and never claims a common cause for their location. Two spellings of "Pisot" appear: the trinomial-roots form of (5), (9), (10), (11) and the minimal-polynomial form of the siegel hypothesis; they coincide exactly when the defining trinomial is irreducible (Selmer for (5), (11); x^3 - x^2 - 1 and x^4 - x^3 - 1 have no rational root and no integer quadratic factorization, for (9), (10)). On the sister family x^m - x^(m-1) - 1 the classes come apart: b_2 = phi and b_5 = rho exactly, so morphic only for m = 2, 5 (AFK, kernel-held, plus strict decrease); Pisot at m = 2, 5 is elementary, though at m = 5 the quintic is reducible with two roots ON the unit circle, so b_5 is Pisot in the minimal-polynomial sense only; the m = 3, 4 members are the kernel-held witnesses; not Pisot for 6 <= m <= 30 numerically and for all m >= 6 Siegel-conditionally (b_6 < rho). The n <= 4 instances of this boundary are registered content of the author's sibling entries (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004, PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005, and PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000008) and are cited as context imports, never re-compared. The classical route to the n >= 4 strict excess (Smyth 1971), the limit behavior of the family measures (Lawton 1983, Smyth 1981, Verger-Gaugry 2016, Stankov 2014), and the outside-root count (Howell-Kyle 2018, with Brilleslyper-Schaubroeck 2014 for the unimodular criterion and Stankov 2014 for the asymptotic density) are cited context, not formalized — see the labeled context block in the sources. As of the 2026-09-01 sweep the entry is not aware of a prior formalization of the general-n family boundary, of Siegel minimality, of Smyth's nonreciprocal bound, or of Pisot-number theory in any surveyed prover ecosystem; Mathlib supplies Selmer irreducibility and the Mahler-measure development as infrastructure. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

(11) The golden quartic root is NOT Pisot: for q^4 = q + 1, some complex root of x^4 = x + 1 other than q has modulus > 1 (every nonreal root does — quartic_conj_norm_gt_one in the proof module, not compared) — with (10) and (7) the degree-4 separation: Q and psi are both algebraic units with constant term of modulus one (unit-ness is elementary and not compared: Q^-1 = Q^3 - 1, psi^-1 = psi^3 - psi^2), yet Q is not Pisot and psi is, so the unit condition alone does not locate the Pisot boundary. (10) and (11) are not independent evidence: x^4 - x^3 - 1 is the image of x^4 - x - 1 under x -> -1/x, so the Pisot half of (10) says x^4 - x - 1 has one root inside the unit circle and three outside, and (11) follows; they are compared separately for the two families' sakes. THE STORY: one shared lemma beneath both boundaries (naming the family-specific arithmetic core, not the whole proof graph: (2) and (6) also share the elementary descent r_n < 1.23 < rho, and the kernel-held Pisot side is localized by Siegel plus descent, the angle route being context); the boundaries localize by different routes — an angle for Pisot (the escape arc between the primitive cube roots of unity, giving the outside-root count 1 + 2*floor((2n - 1)/6), Howell-Kyle 2018 Theorem 3 via the reciprocal trinomial; context, NOT formalized), a degree for morphic (the cofactor x^2 - x + 1 forcing k = 3; formalized) — and the classes are in fact separable: (9)-(11) hold the witnesses and the degree-4 separation in the kernel, with no Siegel input, showing the classes coming apart inside the sister trinomial family itself (Pisot units below phi that are not morphic). The entry never claims the two boundaries are independent (they share the lemma) and never claims a common cause for their location. Two spellings of "Pisot" appear: the trinomial-roots form of (5), (9), (10), (11) and the minimal-polynomial form of the siegel hypothesis; they coincide exactly when the defining trinomial is irreducible (Selmer for (5), (11); x^3 - x^2 - 1 and x^4 - x^3 - 1 have no rational root and no integer quadratic factorization, for (9), (10)). records.name: rank_freeProduct_eq_add
records.entry_name: Grushko--Neumann rank additivity for free products
records.doc: Formalizes the binary Grushko--Neumann theorem: the minimal number of generators of a free product of two finitely generated groups is the sum of the minimal numbers of generators of the factors. The central theorem is proved by a kernel-checked finite labelled-graph reduction. For a minimal null path, the implemented reduction uniformly performs a source unfold, a subsequent safe fold, and an explicit monochromatic-vertex contraction; this gives the strict decrease used by strong induction and the separated-generator lower bound. The repository also retains the finite-core and free-group rank lemmas from the surrounding development as reusable supporting infrastructure, but only the global Grushko theorem declaration is selected by the public Challenge and Comparator.

records.name: Challenge.generalizedMarkoff_reduction_surjective_of_large_prime
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the generic branch of eventual strong approximation for generalized Markoff surfaces, specialized to a fixed ordered integral coefficient triple. It proves punctured transitivity for both the full Vieta group and the two-Vieta rotation group, supplies an explicit coefficient-dependent cutoff, and derives surjectivity of coordinatewise reduction onto the full finite-field surface.

records.name: ExtremalFlagBetti.ActualHomology.flagD1_flagD2
records.entry_name: Actual F₂ flag homology and the dense extremal counterexample family
records.doc: A finite-chain formalization of the F₂ content of Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 3.1 in the source paper. Lean defines the literal flag-chain groups of a finite graph using unordered edges and three-vertex clique faces, their d1 and d2 maps, and actual H1 as ker(d1)/range(d2). It proves that the paper's family G_n has F₂ first Betti number exactly two for every n at least seven, proves the universal F₂ upper bound beta1 <= 2 for every n-vertex graph with choose(n,2)-n edges, and bundles these facts with the exact density and no-complete-bipartite-spanning obstruction. The literal d1-d2 identity is also selected so every Challenge proof hole is compared. No compared proof uses native_decide or an external homology axiom.

records.name: SalemTheorem.salem_theorem
records.entry_name: Salem's theorem: every Pisot number is a two-sided limit of Salem numbers
records.doc: Kernel-checked Salem's theorem — every Pisot number is a limit point of Salem numbers from both sides (R. Salem, Algebraic Numbers and Fourier Analysis, D. C. Heath, 1963, Ch. III, Theorem IV, p. 30; origin R. Salem, Duke Math. J. 12 (1945)) — with both of Salem's constructions, each stated as a construction. Three compared statements carry the surface. (1) salem_theorem — the theorem for Pisot numbers: a real algebraic integer alpha > 1 every other complex root of whose minimal polynomial has modulus < 1 (spelled as 1 < alpha, IsIntegral Z alpha, and every z in (minpoly Q alpha).aroots C other than alpha has norm < 1 — the spelling of the Pisot predicate in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, inlined) has, for every eps > 0, a Salem number in (alpha - eps, alpha) and one in (alpha, alpha + eps). (2) salem_construction_two_sided — Salem's main construction z^m P(z) ± z^p P(1/z) with its family root in the conclusion: for the pattern data of a monic integer polynomial P (one real root alpha > 1, every other complex root strictly inside the unit circle, conjugation-closed) under the nondegeneracy P(1/alpha) != 0 — a proviso that on the pattern domain is strictly STRONGER than Boyd's — coinciding, when P is the minimal polynomial, with Boyd's "provided P is not a reciprocal quadratic" (Math. Comp. 32 (1978), p. 1252, eq. (26)) and with the reason clause of Salem's, "so that Q and P will not be identical" (Salem's stated hypothesis, "theta not a quadratic unit", is stronger; fidelity (g)) — there is a sign e = ±1, the sign of P(1/alpha), such that for every eps > 0 some X^m P + e P.reverse with m >= 2 has a Salem root in (alpha - eps, alpha) and some X^m P - e P.reverse with m >= 2 has a Salem root in (alpha, alpha + eps); P.reverse is z^p P(1/z), p = deg P. (3) salem_quadratic_unit — the excluded case, Salem's second construction (1963, p. 31) with its family root in the conclusion: for the reciprocal quadratic Pisot units alpha^2 = r alpha - 1, r >= 3 an integer, and every eps > 0, some (X^2 - rX + 1)(X^{2m} + 1) + X^{m+1} with m >= 1 has a Salem root in (alpha - eps, alpha) and some (X^2 - rX + 1)(X^{2m} + 1) - X^{m+1} with m >= 1 has a Salem root in (alpha, alpha + eps) — the Chebyshev family (x - r) T_m(x) ∓ 1 pulled back through x = y + 1/y. Statement (1) is the theorem; (2) and (3) each carry their construction and neither follows from (1), their conclusions naming a root of a specific polynomial; Boyd's "for all sufficiently large m" is NOT stated — (2) and (3) assert, per eps, the existence of some index m. A Salem number is spelled by Salem's definition of the class T (1963, p. 26): a real algebraic integer tau > 1 all of whose other conjugates lie in the closed unit disk, at least one on the unit circle — with the clause that 1/tau is a conjugate stated explicitly. Classically that clause and "degree at least 4" are consequences (Salem 1963, p. 26; Smyth 2015, Lemma 1); the equivalence is NOT formalized here, and the formal predicate is the stronger conjunction, which is the CONCLUSION of every compared statement — nothing is assumed of it. THE ROUTE: (1) is transported from a pattern-form theorem in the proof modules (salem_theorem_full), stated for any monic integer polynomial with the pattern data — a larger index set than the Pisot numbers (X^k times a minimal polynomial has the pattern) but equivalent in content, since the large root of any pattern polynomial is itself a Pisot number — through the bridge that the minimal polynomial over Z of a Pisot number carries the pattern data (the Gauss step: the minimal polynomial over Q is the rational image of the one over Z, since Z is integrally closed; separability of the irreducible minimal polynomial in characteristic zero; conjugation-invariance of integer coefficients). The pattern-form theorem splits on P(1/alpha) = 0: the nonzero branch is the assembly PdtSalemEndgame.salem_two_sided; the zero branch reduces to PdtSalemQuadUnit.salem_two_sided_quad_unit by a supporting lemma (reciprocal_quadratic_of_inv_root: a pattern polynomial vanishing at 1/alpha forces alpha^2 = r alpha - 1 with r >= 3 — the elementary "reciprocal Pisot implies quadratic", McKee–Smyth 2012, Lemma 6.2). Those two assemblies discard the index and the family; (2) and (3) are the same assemblies re-run in the bridge module SalemPisot with both kept. The book runs Case 1 under the proviso and handles the quadratic units in Case 2; the kernel unifies both cases in a single statement with no nondegeneracy hypothesis — a presentational unification of Salem's own two cases, not a mathematical strengthening of the theorem, which has no gap. The proofs use no argument principle and no Rouché theorem: the circle counts (m + p - 2 unimodular roots for the plus family z^m P + z^p P(1/z) with p = deg P, m + p - 3 plus the root z = 1 for the minus family, 2m for the quadratic-unit family) are intermediate-value arguments on explicit real phases; the trichotomy (every root unimodular or in {tau, 1/tau}) is a multiset squeeze against the degree; Salem-ness is an arithmetic certificate (the minimal polynomial divides the family; the Gauss step excludes degrees 1 and 2 and forces 1/tau a conjugate), with the integer degeneracies tau in Z and tau + 1/tau in Z discharged by finiteness along the ladders, or directly for the quadratic-unit family. NOT formalized: the equivalence of the Salem-number definitions (above); Boyd's converse (Boyd 1977: every Salem number arises from the construction); Salem 1944 (the Pisot numbers form a closed set); any rate of approach; Boyd's "for all sufficiently large m". As of the 2026-09-01 sweep (Mathlib at the pin and at master, Loogle, the Isabelle AFP at title/abstract/filename level, Coq, HOL Light, Metamath, arXiv; GitHub native code search and Mizar not run) the entry is not aware of a prior formalization of Salem's theorem or of Salem numbers in any surveyed prover ecosystem; the one adjacent hit is the IsPisot definition in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (the definition and the golden-ratio instance; no Salem numbers), whose spelling the compared statement adopts. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

records.name: NashEmbeddingTheorem.nash_isometric_embedding
records.entry_name: Nash's isometric embedding theorem for closed manifolds (Günther's proof)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Nash's C^∞ isometric embedding theorem for closed manifolds: every compact smooth manifold without boundary, equipped with a smooth Riemannian metric, admits a smooth injective map into some Euclidean space ℝ^q whose differential pulls the Euclidean inner product back to the given metric. The proof formalized is Günther's (1989), which replaces the Nash-Moser iteration by an elliptic fixed-point argument, following the presentation in A. J. Wassermann's Cambridge Part III lecture notes as the primary source. The development has two layers. The first proves the theorem for the flat torus: a self-contained Sobolev toolkit on 𝕋ⁿ (weighted ℓ² Sobolev spaces on ℤⁿ, Rellich compactness, the Sobolev sup bound, three multiplication theorems, mollifiers, periodization, Fourier inversion and Parseval), the approximation of smooth metrics by realizable ones, Günther's perturbation theorem proved by a contraction in Hˢ, and their assembly into the statement that every smooth 2π-periodic positive-definite matrix field on ℝⁿ is the pullback metric of a smooth periodic immersion that is injective modulo 2πℤⁿ. The second layer reduces the closed-manifold case to the torus: a Whitney embedding from Mathlib is extended to the ambient space, the metric is extended by a pseudo-inverse construction, cut off, symmetrized and periodized, and the torus theorem is applied. No bound on the embedding dimension is claimed. Concrete instances (round spheres of every dimension, products of spheres, the flat torus 𝕊¹ × 𝕊¹) are derived, and the flat-torus instance is shown to reproduce the torus theorem's conclusion, tying the two layers together. Nothing here is claimed to be new.

records.name: DeBruijnErdos.de_bruijn_erdos
records.entry_name: The De Bruijn–Erdős Theorem on Incidence Geometry and Near-Pencil Tightness
records.doc: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the De Bruijn–Erdős theorem (1948) in incidence geometry and pairwise balanced block designs, together with its constructive near-pencil tightness proof. Proves that any finite linear space on n ≥ 3 non-collinear points determines at least n lines (|P| ≤ |L|) via the classical combinatorial double-counting inequality. records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the full-sequence quantitative theorem for G(n,1/2): with probability tending to one, the chromatic number minus the cochromatic number is at least ((log 2)^2/4) log(200/153) times n/(log n)^3. records.name: PalomarSignedCirculant.periodic_signing_beats_twisted_class
records.entry_name: An explicit periodic signing of C_n(1,2) below the conjectured minimum
records.doc: The paper's disproof of Suvagiya's signed-circulant minimum conjecture on an infinite arithmetic progression, formalized at the matrix level. For every n divisible by 8, Lean defines the paper's period-8 triangle-flux signing of the circulant graph C_n(1,2) as an explicit signed adjacency matrix, proves it is a plus-minus-one signing of mathlib's circulant graph, and proves by exact rational sum-of-squares window certificates that every eigenvalue has absolute value at most 1397/500. For every n >= 32 this rational separator lies strictly below the conjectured minimum rho_-(n) = 2*sqrt(cos^2(pi/n)+cos^2(2pi/n)), so the conjectured value is beaten by an explicit signing on all of n = 0 mod 8, n >= 32. The full Bloch determinant identity and the all-phase algebraic band-edge certificate remain selected as the supporting layer.

records.name: MeanValueForRandomIdealLattices.Palomar.conditionalMainTheorem
records.entry_name: Mean Value for Random Ideal Lattices: Lean formalization
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the geometric, analytic, and arithmetic argument for mean values of lattice-point counts in Haar-random unit-covolume ideal lattices. For cyclotomic fields, it proves the conditional quantitative estimate for every exponent below the assumed subconvexity exponent and its positive power-saving corollary, uniformly over origin-centered balls. The subconvexity, Stark residue, and discriminant-growth inputs remain explicit hypotheses rather than claimed consequences of the formalization.

records.name: Besicovitch.sigma_one_plane_le_6934_div_10000
records.entry_name: A machine-checked bound of 0.6934 for Besicovitch's 1/2-problem
records.doc:
Besicovitch's 1/2-conjecture asserts that a Borel set in the plane with finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure whose lower density exceeds 1/2 almost everywhere is countably 1-rectifiable. Writing sigma_1(R^2) for the least threshold that forces countable 1-rectifiability, the conjecture is sigma_1(R^2) = 1/2. The previously published record is sigma_1(R^2) <= 7/10, obtained by De Lellis, Glaudo, Massaccesi and Vittone.
This development proves, with a complete Lean 4 proof term, sigma_1(R^2) <= 6934/10000 = 0.6934.

records.name: HeilbronnChallenge.heilbronn_convex_three_upper_bound
records.doc:
For n = 3 through n = 8, this formalization determines the supremal minimum triangle area among n indexed planar points whose own convex hull has Lebesgue area one. It proves a pointwise upper bound, attainment, and the exact value for every n in that range. The values are 1, 1/2, (5-sqrt(5))/10, 1/6, 1/9, and, at n = 8, the unique root in (79/1000, 81/1000) of 2060x^5 - 2332x^4 + 1064x^3 - 240x^2 + 26x - 1.
For n = 3, 4, 5, 6, and 8 it also proves pairwise uniqueness of optimizers modulo arbitrary relabeling and arbitrary nonsingular affine transformations. Uniqueness is false at n = 7; instead, an explicit real family is proved to attain throughout its full parameter interval and to exhaust all unit-hull optimizers up to the same equivalence. A real subinterval is pairwise inequivalent, exhibiting a continuum-parameterized set of optimizer orbits; an explicit countable subfamily is retained too.
The n = 3 and n = 4 cases are elementary folklore. The sharp n = 6 and n = 7 values were published by Dress-Yang-Zeng and Yang-Zeng, respectively; the Lean developments here independently reprove those results rather than formalizing the published arguments. The full n = 5 result, the explicit n = 7 family and optimizer classification, and the exact n = 8 result and optimizer classification are first presented in this development. The scoped search described below located prior candidate records but no published full n = 5 proof, no prior exhaustive n = 7 optimizer classification, and no published n = 8 proof. This is not an absolute priority claim. These results are intended for researchers in discrete and computational geometry studying extremal configurations, exact geometric bounds, and formalized combinatorial geometry.

For n = 3 through n = 8, this formalization determines the supremal minimum triangle area among n indexed planar points whose own convex hull has Lebesgue area one. It proves a pointwise upper bound, attainment, and the exact value for every n in that range. The values are 1, 1/2, (5-sqrt(5))/10, 1/6, 1/9, and, at n = 8, the unique root in (79/1000, 81/1000) of 2060x^5 - 2332x^4 + 1064x^3 - 240x^2 + 26x - 1.
For n = 3, 4, 5, 6, and 8 it also proves pairwise uniqueness of optimizers modulo arbitrary relabeling and arbitrary nonsingular affine transformations. Uniqueness is false at n = 7; instead, an explicit real family is proved to attain throughout its full parameter interval and to exhaust all unit-hull optimizers up to the same equivalence. A real subinterval is pairwise inequivalent, exhibiting a continuum-parameterized set of optimizer orbits; an explicit countable subfamily is retained too.
The n = 3 and n = 4 cases are elementary folklore. The sharp n = 6 and n = 7 values were published by Dress-Yang-Zeng and Yang-Zeng, respectively; the Lean developments here independently reprove those results rather than formalizing the published arguments. The full n = 5 result, the explicit n = 7 family and optimizer classification, and the exact n = 8 result and optimizer classification are first presented in this development. The scoped search described below located prior candidate records but no published full n = 5 proof, no prior exhaustive n = 7 optimizer classification, and no published n = 8 proof. This is not an absolute priority claim. These results are intended for researchers in discrete and computational geometry studying extremal configurations, exact geometric bounds, and formalized combinatorial geometry.

records.name: Propositions.riemann_roch
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Baker and Norine's Riemann-Roch theorem for finite graphs. Chip configurations on a finite graph, modulo chip-firing moves, form an abelian group analogous to the group of line bundles on a compact Riemann surface. Each class can be assigned a rank, analogous to the dimension of a linear series. These ranks then satisfy a formula of the form r(D) - r(K-D) = deg D + 1 - g, in exact analogy to Riemann surfaces. This formula is formalized, along with the analog of Clifford's theorem for finite graphs.
