records.name: TraceForms.trace_tmul
records.entry_name: The trace form of a tensor product of algebras and the signature product rule, with the trace forms of Q[x]/(x^3 - x - 1), Q[x]/(x^4 - x - 1) and their compositum as instances
records.doc: GENERAL THEOREMS FIRST. For finite free algebras A, B over a commutative ring R, the trace form of the tensor product A ⊗_R B is the tensor product of the trace forms, and over a linearly ordered field the Sylvester signature of a tensor product of quadratic forms obeys a product rule. Seven compared general statements: (1) the trace of a pure tensor is the product of the traces, Tr_{A⊗B}(a ⊗ b) = Tr_A(a)·Tr_B(b); (2) the trace form on pure tensors is the product of the trace forms; (3) the Gram matrix of a tensor basis bA ⊗ bB (Mathlib's Basis.tensorProduct) is the Kronecker product of the two Gram matrices; (4) the discriminant product formula WITH SIGN, disc(bA ⊗ bB) = disc(bA)^|kappa| · disc(bB)^|iota| for bases indexed by finite types iota, kappa; (5) when 2 is invertible in R, the trace quadratic form of A ⊗ B is the tensor product (Mathlib's QuadraticForm.tmul) of the trace quadratic forms; (6)-(7) THE SIGNATURE PRODUCT RULE: over a linearly ordered field with 2 invertible, for quadratic forms Q1, Q2 on finite-dimensional spaces, sigPos(Q1 ⊗ Q2) = p1 p2 + n1 n2 and sigNeg(Q1 ⊗ Q2) = p1 n2 + n1 p2, with sigPos/sigNeg Mathlib's basis-free invariants (maximal dimension of a positive- resp. negative-definite subspace). (6)-(7) are the (p, n)-refinement of the multiplicativity of the signature homomorphism on the Witt ring of an ordered field (Lam 2005, Chapter VIII), stated for arbitrary (possibly degenerate) forms and proved by orthogonal bases and the uniqueness half of Sylvester's law. The Witt-ring statement gives only the difference p - n; recovering p and n separately for a possibly degenerate tensor product would in addition need the dimension of the radical of a tensor product, which Mathlib does not have either; the entry proves the two counts directly, without the Witt ring, which is not formalized. None of (1)-(7) was in Mathlib at the pin; Mathlib's nearest results are the trace of a tensor product of endomorphisms (LinearMap.trace_tensorProduct'), the determinant of a Kronecker product, the tensor product of quadratic forms and its polar form, orthogonal bases, and sigPos/sigNeg with Sylvester uniqueness — the infrastructure from which (1)-(7) are built. PRIOR ART on (4): Mathlib at the pin has NumberField.natAbs_discr_eq_natAbs_discr_pow_mul_natAbs_discr_pow — for two linearly disjoint number fields with coprime different ideals the ABSOLUTE VALUE of the discriminant of their compositum is |d1|^[K2:Q]·|d2|^[K1:Q] (via the different; the classical statement is in Khanduja 2019). Statement (4) is the elementary basis-level version: any finite free algebras over any commutative ring, the exact signed discriminant of the tensor basis, with no number-field, integrality or coprimality hypothesis; it neither implies nor is implied by the Mathlib theorem, and is cited beside it. THE INSTANCES (8)-(23), at the two fields cut out by the trinomials x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1 — the cubic and quartic members of the family x^n - x - 1, irreducible over the rationals for every n >= 2 by Selmer's theorem (Mathlib), whose real roots above 1 are the plastic number and the quartic root of x^4 = x + 1 — and their compositum. The trace form of a number field K of degree n is (x, y) -> Tr(xy); in the power basis 1, x, ..., x^(n-1) its Gram matrix is the Hankel matrix (Tr x^(i+j)) of the power sums of the roots. (8)-(9) The Gram matrices, entrywise: Algebra.traceMatrix of the power family equals the explicit integer Hankel matrix — power sums 3, 0, 2, 3, 2 for the cubic and 4, 0, 0, 3, 4, 0, 3 for the quartic, from Newton's identities on the coefficients. (10)-(11) The discriminants of the power bases, Algebra.discr of the same families: -23 and -283, both prime. (12)-(13) Explicit diagonalisations: the trace form, as a quadratic form, is equivalent to the weighted sum of squares with weights 3, 2, -23/6 resp. 4, 4, -9/4, 283/36 — one congruence among many, exhibited with its rational change of basis. (14)-(17) The Sylvester signatures as basis-free invariants: sigPos and sigNeg are 2 and 1 for the cubic trace form and 3 and 1 for the quartic, read off from (12)-(13) through Sylvester uniqueness. (18)-(23) THE COMPOSITUM: the tensor product L = K_3 ⊗_Q K_4 is their compositum Q(rho, Q) — the degrees 3 and 4 are coprime, so the fields are linearly disjoint and L is a field, statement (23), from Mathlib's coprime-degree linear-disjointness criterion — and (18)-(22) are the general theorems at this pair: Tr(x ⊗ y) = Tr(x)·Tr(y); the Gram matrix of the tensor power family x^i ⊗ y^j (Fin 3 × Fin 4) is the Kronecker product of the two Gram matrices; the discriminant of that family is (-23)^4·(-283)^3 by (4); the Sylvester signature is (7, 5) by (6)-(7) applied to (2, 1) and (3, 1) — agreeing with the classical (r_1 + r_2, r_2) for the compositum's two real and five complex places (context, not compared). The registered compositum entry PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005 treats the same field as Q(rho·Q), through the degree-12 minimal polynomial of the product; that Q(rho, Q) = Q(rho·Q) follows by degree count and is context here, never compared. THE CLASSICAL SETTING of the instances: the trace form of a number field with r_1 real and r_2 pairs of complex embeddings has signature (r_1 + r_2, r_2) — for the Hankel form of a polynomial this is Hermite's 1856 theorem (the signature difference counts the distinct real roots), and for the discriminant matrix of a number field it is Taussky's 1968 note; Conner and Perlis's 1984 survey is the standard reference. Here (r_1, r_2) = (1, 1), (2, 1) and (2, 5), so the classical theorem predicts exactly (2, 1), (3, 1) and (7, 5), and the Hermite counts 2 - 1 = 1 and 3 - 1 = 2 match the real-root counts of the two trinomials. That general theorem is NOT formalized: the two-field instances are proved directly by explicit congruence, the compositum instance by the general theorems (1)-(7); the embedding counts r_1, r_2 appear in no compared statement. WHY THESE FIELDS, for the instances: the cubic field is the signature-[1, 1] cubic field of smallest absolute discriminant (LMFDB, sorted by |disc|: 3.1.23.1 first, then 3.1.31.1); its Galois closure is the Artin field of the weight-one newform 23.1.b.a = eta(z) eta(23z), the classical Hecke example with Artin image S_3, whose analytic conductor the LMFDB records as minimal among all classical newforms and whose Stark unit is the root of x^3 - x - 1 itself; its integral trace form — which the compared Gram matrix (8) is, the power basis being an integral basis — is the object of Mantilla-Soler's study of integral trace forms of cubic fields (Algebra & Number Theory 2010). The quartic field is the degree-4 member of the same trinomial family, registered as the degree-4 Mahler-measure minimizer (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004), with the same profile: prime discriminant, monogenic. The field discriminants: the LMFDB records 4.2.283.1 (defining polynomial x^4 - x - 1, signature [2, 1], discriminant -283, monogenic, index 1) and 3.1.23.1 (reduced defining polynomial x^3 - x^2 + 1, the field generated by -1/rho, signature [1, 1], discriminant -23, monogenic, index 1) list -283 and -23 as the field discriminants; that the power bases are integral bases, so that the compared power-basis discriminants ARE the field discriminants, is cited from those records and not formalized; likewise the tensor power family is an integral basis of the compositum because the two discriminants are coprime (the standard integral-basis theorem for linearly disjoint fields; context only). PRIOR ART on the instances, as of the 2026-09-02 sweep: Mathlib contains no trace-form or discriminant computation for either field. The nearest prior work is the Lean 4 certification framework of Baanen, Chavarri Villarello and Dahmen (CPP 2025) and its 2026 sequel (Chavarri Villarello and Dahmen): they certify rings of integers, FIELD discriminants (as the determinant of the trace matrix of a certified integral basis) and, in the sequel, the signature (r_1, r_2) by real-root counting, for LMFDB entries at large; neither treats the trace form's Sylvester signature, and their published example sets (seven non-monogenic cubic fields unramified outside 2, 3, 5 in the first; the v1 example directory of the second) contain neither of the two fields here (checked 2026-09-02). Relative to that work, the compared discriminants (10)-(11) are the power-basis discriminants derived from the explicit Gram matrices — a weaker notion than the certified field discriminant, which coincides with it here because both fields are monogenic (LMFDB, cited) — and the Sylvester signatures have no counterpart there. The entry is not aware of a formalization, in any surveyed prover ecosystem, of the trace form of a tensor product of algebras, of the signature product rule, or of a number field's trace-form Sylvester signature. The proof modules descend from the author's public pdt-lean development (pinned below), where none of these statements was ever a compared statement. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

records.name: ore_hamiltonian
records.entry_name: Ore's and Dirac's Theorems on Hamiltonian Cycles

records.name: ConwayRefinement.Palomar.conwayRefinement
records.entry_name: A proof of Conway's refinement conjecture
records.doc: A Lean proof of Conway's 1976 refinement conjecture for omnific integers. For omnific integers a, b, c, d with ab = cd, it proves the existence of omnific integers e, f, g, h satisfying a = ef, b = gh, c = eg, and d = fh, including zero and degenerate cases. The proof proceeds through factorisation and refinement theory for generalised-power-series integer parts and connects the generalised-power-series and surreal-number formulations.

records.name: TverbergsTheorem.tverbergs_theorem
records.entry_name: Tverberg's Partition Theorem, 1D Theorem, and Colorful 1D Theorem
records.doc: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Tverberg's Theorem (Helge Tverberg, 1966) in the distinct-point set formulation across dimensions d >= 1 (with d = 0, r > 1 cases vacuously satisfied due to Finset carrier capacity limits on Fin 0 -> ℝ) via the Sarkaria–Bárány Colorful Carathéodory reduction, the full 1D Tverberg theorem for arbitrary r via symmetric-rank pairing following Mulzer–Werner, and the 1-dimensional Colorful Tverberg Theorem for arbitrary r (Bárány–Larman–Pach 1992). Proves that any (r - 1)(d + 1) + 1 points in ℝ^d can be partitioned into r parts whose convex hulls intersect, and that two disjoint color classes of r points each in ℝ¹ can be partitioned into r colorful pairs whose convex hulls share a common point of intersection. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.name: EhrenfestArgument.harmonicOnNhd_radial_iff
records.entry_name: Radial harmonic functions on a real inner product space: the classification, the Laplacian of radial functions, and the stability of circular orbits for power-law central forces; Ehrenfest's dimensionality argument (1917) as the application
records.doc: GENERAL THEOREMS FIRST. Throughout, E is a finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension n, Δ is Mathlib's coordinate-free Laplacian, HarmonicOnNhd its harmonic functions, and f : ℝ → ℝ is twice differentiable on (0, ∞) (two HasDerivAt hypotheses, with derivatives f', f''). (I) THE CLASSIFICATION OF RADIAL HARMONIC FUNCTIONS: (1) for n ≠ 2 and E ≠ 0, the radial function f ∘ ‖·‖ is harmonic on E ∖ {0} if and only if f(r) = a + b r^(2−n) on (0, ∞) for some real a, b; (2) for n = 2, if and only if f(r) = a + b log r — every radial harmonic function with a twice-differentiable profile is an affine function of the Newtonian potential, constants included, and of the logarithm in the plane. (II) THE LAPLACIAN OF RADIAL FUNCTIONS, away from the origin: (3) Δ(f ∘ ‖·‖)(x) = f''(‖x‖) + (n − 1) f'(‖x‖)/‖x‖, the radial Laplacian; (4) for g twice differentiable on (0, ∞), Δ(g(‖y‖²))(x) = 2n g'(‖x‖²) + 4‖x‖² g''(‖x‖²), the squared-norm parametrization; (5) for every real s, Δ(‖y‖^s)(x) = s (n + s − 2) ‖x‖^(s−2), the indicial identity (its consequence, not itself compared: for E ≠ 0, ‖y‖^s is harmonic away from 0 exactly when s (n + s − 2) = 0, at s = 0 and s = 2 − n, which coincide at n = 2); (6) Δ(log ‖y‖)(x) = (n − 2)/‖x‖²; (7) ‖y‖^(2−n) is harmonic on E ∖ {0} for every n — for n ≥ 3, up to its normalizing constant, the Newtonian kernel away from the origin (the normalization and the distributional identity −ΔΦ = δ at the origin, in Evans's sign convention, which make a normalized multiple of it the fundamental solution proper, are NOT formalized); at n = 2 the power is the constant 1 and the logarithmic case is (8); on the zero space the statement is vacuous; (8) log ‖y‖ is harmonic on E ∖ {0} when n = 2. (III) THE RADIAL EQUATION, the one-variable content of (1)-(2): (9) for n ≠ 2, f'' + (n − 1) f'/r = 0 on (0, ∞) if and only if f(r) = a + b r^(2−n) there for some a, b; (10) for n = 2, if and only if f(r) = a + b log r. (IV) THE STABILITY OF CIRCULAR ORBITS, general in the real exponent: for the effective potential U(r) = a/r² − b/r^p on (0, ∞), a, b > 0, p > 0 real — the radial potential of a body with angular momentum under a central attraction with force law 1/r^(p+1) — (11) U'(r) = 0 iff r^(2−p) = 2a/(bp), the circular-orbit condition (for p ≠ 2 that equation has exactly one positive solution, whence "the circular orbit" below — a consequence of (11), not itself compared; in the plane "the circular orbit r = √(2a/b)" names the point of (19)); (12) at a circular orbit U''(r) = 2a(2 − p)/r⁴; (13) for p < 2 the circular orbit r* = (2a/(bp))^(1/(2−p)) is a local minimum of U (Mathlib's non-strict IsLocalMin) — stable; (14) for p > 2 it is a local maximum — unstable; (15) for p > 2 U has no local minimum on (0, ∞) at all (Ehrenfest's reading, that bounded motion between two radii is then impossible, is not formalized); (16) U''(r*) r*⁴/(2a) = 2 − p, the square of the ratio of the radial to the angular frequency of small oscillations about the circular orbit, which the local step of Bertrand's argument requires to be the square of a rational number for a near-circular orbit to close. The boundary p = 2, where the two terms of U have the same power, is covered by the critical-point and second-derivative identities (11)-(12), whose only hypothesis on the exponent is p > 0, and is excluded from the stability conclusions (13)-(15) and the frequency identity (16), all of which require p ≠ 2; among the instances it is n = 4, where (17) with a ≠ b yields no local minimum (the potential (a − b)/r² has no critical point) while the sub-case a = b, where U vanishes, is excluded; the table's 'unstable' cell at n = 4 is not compared. THE INSTANCES (17)-(23), with p = n − 2 for the Newtonian potential in n ≥ 3 dimensions and the logarithmic potential in the plane: (17) for n ≥ 3 and a ≠ b a stable circular orbit exists iff n = 3 (a ≠ b excludes n = 4, a = b, where U vanishes identically and every point is a non-strict minimum); (18) for n ≥ 5 the effective potential has no local minimum on (0, ∞); (19) in the plane, for a/r² + b log r, the circular orbit r = √(2a/b) is stable; (20) the quantity of (16) is 4 − n for n ≥ 3, n ≠ 4, hence 1 at n = 3; (21) in the plane it equals 2; (22) in the plane its square root is irrational (it is √2 by (21); this statement asserts irrationality only); (23) ‖x‖^(2−n) is harmonic on ℝⁿ ∖ {0} for every n; for n ≥ 3, up to its normalizing constant, the Newtonian kernel away from the origin, with the same disclosure as (7). THE APPLICATION: Ehrenfest's argument of 1917 (KNAW Proceedings 20 (1918) 200-209, §1 and Appendix I) that the stability of planetary orbits singles out three spatial dimensions. He deduces the n-dimensional force law from the Laplace–Poisson equation (the Laplace half is statement (7), harmonicity away from the source; the Poisson half, the point source, is not formalized; the classification (1)-(2) makes "the radial harmonic function" a theorem), reduces the motion to the radial equation ṙ = (1/r)√(A r² + B r^(4−n) − C²), and tabulates three columns — circular trajectories; motions between two positive values of r; motion to the infinite — for n ≥ 4 (unstable, impossible, possible), n = 3 (stable, possible and moreover closed, possible), n = 2 (stable, possible and not closed, impossible). Statements (17)-(22) are the extrema and frequency identities of the effective potential behind the first two columns for n ≥ 5, n = 3, n = 2 — a local minimum where the table says stable, no local minimum where it says bounded motion is impossible, the frequency ratio where it says closed or not closed; the passage from those identities to trajectories (bounded motion, closure, the third column), the n = 4 cell, and Bertrand's global theorem (1873) are not formalized. Tangherlini (1963) extended the argument to the n-dimensional Schwarzschild field; Caruso and Xavier (1987) and Tegmark (1997) discuss its epistemological status and call it Ehrenfest's argument, as does this entry ("Ehrenfest's theorem" names his 1927 quantum-mechanical result). NOT formalized: Bertrand's theorem, the third column and the n = 4 cell of the table, the derivation of the effective potential from the equations of motion, the relativistic extension, the wave-equation half of Ehrenfest's paper (Huygens' principle in odd dimensions), and any statement about the actual dimension of physical space — the theorems classify radial functions and a family of effective potentials; the reading that the stable case is the world we observe is Ehrenfest's, cited, not compared. PRIOR ART, as of the 2026-09-02 sweep: Mathlib has the Laplacian on inner product spaces (InnerProductSpace.laplacian, laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis), harmonic functions (HarmonicAt, HarmonicOnNhd, harmonicAt_congr_nhds) with complex-analytic examples — in particular AnalyticAt.harmonicAt_log_norm, which gives log |z| harmonic on ℂ ∖ {0}, the n = 2 case of (8) in the complex model obtained through complex analysis — the second- derivative test (isLocalMin_of_deriv_deriv_pos), the mean-value lemmas IsOpen.exists_is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero and IsOpen.exists_eq_add_of_deriv_eq, and real powers; it has no Laplacian of a radial function, no harmonic power of the norm, no classification of radial harmonic functions, no central-force mechanics, and no formalization of Ehrenfest's argument. No formalization of the classification of radial harmonic functions, of Ehrenfest's argument, of the harmonic Newtonian potential in general dimension, or of Bertrand's theorem was found in the surveyed prover ecosystems (Mathlib and its archive, the Isabelle AFP, the Coq Mathematical Components and Coquelicot analysis libraries). The proof module descends from the author's public pdt-lean development (pinned below), where none of these statements was ever a compared statement. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

(III) THE RADIAL EQUATION, the one-variable content of (1)-(2): (9) for n ≠ 2, f'' + (n − 1) f'/r = 0 on (0, ∞) if and only if f(r) = a + b r^(2−n) there for some a, b; (10) for n = 2, if and only if f(r) = a + b log r. records.name: EhrenfestArgument.harmonicOnNhd_euclidean
records.entry_name: Radial harmonic functions on a real inner product space: the classification, the Laplacian of radial functions, and the stability of circular orbits for power-law central forces; Ehrenfest's dimensionality argument (1917) as the application
records.doc: GENERAL THEOREMS FIRST. Throughout, E is a finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension n, Δ is Mathlib's coordinate-free Laplacian, HarmonicOnNhd its harmonic functions, and f : ℝ → ℝ is twice differentiable on (0, ∞) (two HasDerivAt hypotheses, with derivatives f', f''). records.name: SharpIntermediateSubgroupBounds.bandwise_moment
records.entry_name: Sharp bounds for intervals in finite subgroup lattices
records.doc: Let H be a subgroup of a finite group G, let n = [G:H] > 1, and let p be the least prime divisor of n. This Lean development proves an exact finite rational upper envelope for the number of subgroups K with H ≤ K ≤ G and the strict bound c(p) n^((log_p n)/4), where c(p) is an Euler-product times a Gaussian theta series. It formalizes the bandwise moment inequality that drives the proof, a universal base-two bound with an exact decimal coefficient, the exact optimal answer for prime-power indices, and elementary-abelian asymptotics showing that both the constant and the exponent 1/4 are optimal.

records.name: Erdos684.Palomar.main_theorem
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 684: f(n)/log n is unbounded — a Lean 4 formalization of arXiv:2604.23784
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization, against Mathlib, of the main theorem of J. H. Bae, "Unbounded logarithmic limsup in Erdős Problem 684 via shifted carry scheduling" (arXiv:2604.23784, v3).  For 0 ≤ k ≤ n write C(n,k) = u·v with u supported on the primes ≤ k and v on the primes in (k,n], and let f(n) be the least k with u > n²; Erdős asked for bounds on f(n) (Problem 684 in Bloom's database).  The compared theorems state that for every ε > 0 there are infinitely many n with f(n) > (1/2 − ε)·log n·log log n / log log log n, equivalently limsup f(n)·log log log n /(log n·log log n) ≥ 1/2 (stated in the extended nonnegative reals), and in particular that f(n)/log n is unbounded, so no estimate f(n) = O(log n) holds.  This strengthens the subsequential lower bound (1/2 − o(1)) log n of Alexeev–Putterman–Sawhney–Sellke–Valiant by a factor of order log log n / log log log n; the general upper bound (log n)² remains the best known and the exact order of f(n) is open.  Two further compared statements fix the meaning of the definitions: u(n,k) times the part of C(n,k) supported on primes exceeding k equals C(n,k), and K < f(n) holds exactly when u(n,k) ≤ n² for all 1 ≤ k ≤ min(K,n).  The proof follows the paper section by section (Kummer carries, a product-cell code, a CRT count with exponential weighting, an anchored-fibre selection lemma, and a four-range carry budget).  The prime number theorem is the single analytic input: the library proves the theorem under the explicit hypothesis θ(x) = x + O(x/log² x) and then discharges that hypothesis from the bound ψ(x) = x + O(x·exp(−c(log x)^{1/10})) of the PrimeNumberTheoremAnd project (Kontorovich, Tao et al.), so the compared theorems carry no hypotheses and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

The proof follows the paper section by section (Kummer carries, a product-cell code, a CRT count with exponential weighting, an anchored-fibre selection lemma, and a four-range carry budget).  The prime number theorem is the single analytic input: the library proves the theorem under the explicit hypothesis θ(x) = x + O(x/log² x) and then discharges that hypothesis from the bound ψ(x) = x + O(x·exp(−c(log x)^{1/10})) of the PrimeNumberTheoremAnd project (Kontorovich, Tao et al.), so the compared theorems carry no hypotheses and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: TuckersLemma.tucker_1d
records.entry_name: Tucker's Lemma: Full Combinatorial & Topological Parity Suite in 1D and 2D
records.doc: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Tucker's Lemma (Albert W. Tucker, 1945) and the combinatorial Borsuk–Ulam theorem in 1D and 2D without artificial conditions. Formalizes four foundational pillars: (1) 1D discrete sign-change parity and antipodal interval subdivision lemma; (2) 2D combinatorial double counting of face doors and modulo-2 parity conservation on edge-pseudomanifolds; (3) the boundary cycle engine on 2D edge-pseudomanifolds with an enumerated cyclic boundary (CyclicBoundaryPseudomanifold2D) under antipodal boundary labeling, proving that non-complementary boundary labelings force odd boundary door parity, thereby establishing the 2D Tucker's Lemma on cyclic boundary pseudomanifolds, retracting previous claims of full topological disk coverage; and (4) the concrete 6-vertex, 8-face, 12-edge octahedral 2-sphere S^2_8 triangulation. All declarations rely strictly on standard Lean 4 kernel axioms (propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice).

records.name: GKEvenNet.net
records.entry_name: Even-order Grünschloß–Keller permutation nets: net property and tiling distance
records.doc: This Lean development proves that the even-order permutation construction of Grünschloß and Keller (MCQMC 2008 proceedings, implemented in gendiag0m2.h) is a base-2 (0,m,2)-net for every even m >= 4. The proof is symbolic: for every resolution a <= m the dyadic-box map is shown injective through the concatenation x = floor(k/4) + 2^(m/2-2) z and fixed-width bit-reversal splitting, and a cardinality argument upgrades injectivity to a bijection (exactly one point per elementary interval). For the source's row-shifted tiling lattice <(N,0),(N/4,N)> it proves, for every even m >= 8, that one explicit pair of points has squared distance 241 * 2^(m-8), and at m = 8 that 241 is the exact minimum over all pairs and all lattice translates. The exhaustive m = 8 lower bound is reduced by ordinary kernel decide; the exactness of the computed candidate minimum over the whole lattice is a symbolic lemma. The all-parameter lower bound of the distance theorem (even m >= 10) is proved in the paper but is not formalized.

records.name: K331Tutte.Bridge.structural_theorem
records.entry_name: Combinatorial core of the K₃,₃,₁-redundancy theorem for tetrahedral balls
records.doc: Alexa's three-dimensional Tutte embedding theorem (Discrete & Computational Geometry, 2025) requires the graph of a tetrahedral mesh to have neither a K₆ nor a K₃,₃,₁ minor and asks whether the second exclusion is necessary. The paper proves that it is redundant for finite simplicial complexes whose realization is a closed topological 3-ball and which satisfy the boundary-triangle condition (BT): if the 1-skeleton G has no K₆ minor, then G is linklessly embeddable and hence has no K₃,₃,₁ minor (Theorem 1.1). This Lean development proves the paper's new combinatorial mathematics over mathlib simple graphs and finite simplicial complexes and composes it into Theorem 1.1 with the cited theorems as explicit hypotheses. Proved: for every four-clique of a (BT) pair the induced relative F₂ chain complex has homology of dimension at most one (Lemma 4.3, with the soundness of its Boolean coordinate model, Lemma 7.1); a K₄-attachment never merges components of the old part (Lemma 5.2); every MP₁-cockade whose four-clique deletions leave at most two components is linklessly embeddable, given the four-clique Holst–Lovász–Schrijver criterion and linkless atoms (Proposition 5.3); and the joined statement structural_theorem, in which the skeleton of the complex is a mathlib SimpleGraph, every skeleton four-clique is a labelled four-clique of the pair, and the hypotheses are Corollary 3.6 (rigidity, Mader, Jørgensen), the relative ball duality of Section 4, Corollary 2.5, and Lemma 5.1. Generic rigidity, the extremal-minor classification, PL duality, the Holst–Lovász–Schrijver theorem, apex linklessness, and Alexa's theorem are not formalized and enter only as named hypotheses.

records.name: Erdos647.erdos647_no_solution_upto_1e8
records.entry_name: A kernel-checked exclusion certificate for Erdős Problem 647, to 10^8
records.doc:
Erdős Problem 647 asks whether there is any n > 24 with max_{m < n} (m + tau(m)) <= n + 2, where tau counts divisors. The value n = 24 satisfies it and the question is open. This entry certifies a bounded exclusion: no such n exists in (24, 10^8]. It does not resolve the problem and asserts nothing about n > 10^8.
The exclusion is certified rather than searched at check time. A witness at a cover position is an offset together with prime-power pairs dividing m, certifying tau(m) >= prod (e + 1); every prime in a pair is below 1024 and is checked prime by eleven trial divisions, so no primality certificates appear anywhere. A chain of witnesses covers the interval and each certificate chunk is discharged by a single decide against the chain checker, so the Lean kernel certifies the arithmetic and the generator that produced it is never trusted.
The audience is the community working on the Erdős problems database and its Lean formalizations, for whom a machine-checked lower bound on the search range is directly usable, and researchers building certificate-based exclusions in elementary number theory, for whom the witness format and its kernel-evaluable checkers are the transferable part.

records.name: ChiralPadovanHistories.return_clock_bounds
records.entry_name: Sharp arithmetic separation in chiral Padovan histories
records.doc: Sixteen compared statements establish quantitative recurrence for the actual infinite Padovan prefix path and compare cubic and quartic arithmetic record windows. For 0<epsilon<=1, every nonempty prefix whose conjugate coordinate lies within epsilon of the origin has expanding coordinate at least epsilon^(-2); an actual prefix returns with expanding coordinate at most r^3*epsilon^(-2). Every letter stream satisfies the pairwise bound abs(Delta X)*norm(Delta W)^2>=1, and Padovan substitution stages attain equality at arbitrarily large clocks. The full cubic record window is relatively dense with uniformly discrete differences; the identical positive-real window in the quartic case admits nonzero inverse-unit points arbitrarily close to zero, while its other real embedding grows. Scalar prefix coordinates factor the included faithful chiral timelike history in the genuine quartic trace geometry. The formalization exposes the return bounds, actual-word attainment, constructive covering, and explicit obstruction as its principal mathematical consequences.

For the derivative image of the Kasami monomial x^(4^k-2^k+1) with gcd(k,n)=1, over a finite field of characteristic two with 2^n elements, the formalized result gives the exact three-variable coefficient count 2^(2n-3) for every pair of distinct nonzero coefficients.

records.name: BNChains.cdpr_marked_no_high_multiplicity
records.entry_name: Brill--Noether generality and gonality for chains of cycles and theta graphs
records.doc: This repository formalizes Brill--Noether generality for chains whose factors may be cycles or theta graphs, subject to a genericity condition on path lengths and an evenly-marked condition on the theta factors. A graph is called Brill--Noether general if the possible degrees and ranks of its chip configurations, in the sense of Baker and Norine, match the behavior of a general algebraic curve. Here we use only the existential form of Brill--Noether generality, without computing dimensions. Following Cools--Draisma--Payne--Robeva, we also formalize a mild vanishing-order condition that permits the recovery of dimension statements on the algebraic side. A Brill--Noether general graph also has the conjectural maximum gonality in its genus. The chain of cycles case is a theorem of Cools--Draisma--Payne--Robeva, which Pflueger--Solomon generalized to allow evenly-marked theta graphs. Among other things, the construction shows the existence, in every positive genus g, of graphs with every gonality between 2 and ceil(g/2) + 1, inclusive.

records.name: Sqrt6KissingBound.kissingConfiguration_card_le_sqrt6_pow
records.entry_name: The optimal universal exponential base for Euclidean kissing numbers
records.doc: For every positive integer n, the Euclidean kissing number tau_n is an attained maximum and satisfies tau_n <= (sqrt(6))^n. This Lean formalization proves the bound by packing explicit bodies of revolution in the unit ball, including the geometric separation, volume integrals, and every dimension case. An explicit six-point planar configuration proves tau_2 = 6. Consequently sqrt(6) is the least nonnegative (and least positive) universal exponential base without a prefactor; the admissible bases are exactly alpha >= sqrt(6), and the supremum of tau_n^(1/n) over positive dimensions equals sqrt(6). No asymptotic-optimality claim is made.

records.name: N4Code.palomar_thm1
records.entry_name: N4Code: optimal finite-length block codes of size four for binary symmetric channels
records.doc: A Lean 4 and mathlib formalization of the Dong-Yang classification of optimal (n,4) binary block codes for binary symmetric channels.  The registered results are Theorems 1-5 of the paper: existence of an optimal linear or Class-I code, the explicit linear optimal codes by residue class modulo 3, the universal strict-improvement reductions outside the linear, Class-I, and Class-II classes, the Class-I condition reduction to linear codes, and the finite classification for blocklengths 2 <= n <= 8. The Lean statements use the strict-improvement contrapositive forms.

records.name: OneTwoSobolT5.exact_t_five_certificate
records.entry_name: Exact four-dimensional projection quality of the OneTwo Sobol' table at 65,536 points
records.doc: The quality parameter t of a base-2 digital net with 2^m points measures exact equidistribution in dyadic boxes, and for Sobol' sequences used in quasi-Monte Carlo integration and computer graphics the quality of low-dimensional projections is a practical bottleneck. The OneTwo construction of Bonneel, Coeurjolly, Iehl, and Ostromoukhov (ACM Transactions on Graphics, 2025) releases a 692-dimension direction-number table whose protected pairs (2k-1, 2k) have the (1,2) property, with acceptance targets t <= 3 through m <= 10 and t <= 4 through m <= 15 for the pair-aligned four-dimensional blocks. Theorem 1.1 of the preprint determines the next depth exactly: at m = 16, a complete batch of 65,536 points, every one of the 345 pair-aligned windows of the released table has exact four-dimensional t-value 4 when its first dimension is one of 1, 7, 31, 49, 67, 195, 225, 243, 373 and t-value 5 otherwise, so the t <= 4 guarantee extends to m = 16 in exactly nine windows and fails in the other 336, each failure witnessed by an empty dyadic box of volume 2^-12 in that projection. The standard star-discrepancy bound for the projection is 299/4096 at t = 4 and 29/256 at t = 5. This Lean development proves the theorem in rank form with the released table embedded as one 256-bit literal per dimension: for every window, every four-part composition at the threshold total selects independent generator rows over F_2 and some composition one total higher does not, and the distribution is 9 windows at t = 4 and 336 at t = 5. The worked block, dimensions 25 to 28, keeps its separate explicit certificate (t = 5, with every smaller threshold refuted). All checks are 16-column XOR row reductions reduced by kernel decide with no native evaluation. The digital-net rank criterion, the discrepancy bound, and the authentication of the upstream table remain informal.

Theorem 1.1 of the preprint determines the next depth exactly: at m = 16, a complete batch of 65,536 points, every one of the 345 pair-aligned windows of the released table has exact four-dimensional t-value 4 when its first dimension is one of 1, 7, 31, 49, 67, 195, 225, 243, 373 and t-value 5 otherwise, so the t <= 4 guarantee extends to m = 16 in exactly nine windows and fails in the other 336, each failure witnessed by an empty dyadic box of volume 2^-12 in that projection. The standard star-discrepancy bound for the projection is 299/4096 at t = 4 and 29/256 at t = 5. The worked block, dimensions 25 to 28, keeps its separate explicit certificate (t = 5, with every smaller threshold refuted). All checks are 16-column XOR row reductions reduced by kernel decide with no native evaluation. The digital-net rank criterion, the discrepancy bound, and the authentication of the upstream table remain informal.

records.name: li_criterion
records.entry_name: Li's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis
records.doc: Li's criterion for the Riemann zeta function, formalized in Lean 4 over Mathlib: Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` holds if and only if every Li-Keiper coefficient of the completed xi function has nonnegative real part. The zero-indexed analytic coefficient at n is Li's classical lambda_(n+1), the n-th Taylor coefficient at 0 of the logarithmic derivative of s |-> xi(1/(1-s)). A second compared theorem identifies this analytic coefficient with Li's arithmetic coefficient, the symmetrized sum over the nontrivial zeros counted with multiplicity, and proves that symmetrized family summable so the sum is the genuine one. Both results are unconditional: the biconditional, the coefficient identification, the genus-1 Hadamard factorization of xi (with multiplicity), genus-1 summability of 1/|rho|^2, and the growth bound order(xi) <= 1 are all proved. This is a formalization of a classically known equivalence (X.-J. Li, 1997); it is not a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, nor of the positivity of the coefficients.

records.name: KroneckerWeber.exists_cyclotomicEmbedding
records.entry_name: The global Kronecker–Weber theorem in Lean 4
records.doc: This project formalizes the global Kronecker–Weber theorem in Lean 4: every finite abelian extension of the rational numbers embeds into a cyclotomic field. For a number field L that is abelian Galois over the rationals, the selected declaration gives a positive integer n and a rational algebra embedding from L into CyclotomicField n ℚ. The proof is supplied by the ClassFieldTheory library at a fixed commit, using Lean 4.33.0 and Mathlib.

records.name: Stafford38Challenge.universalStatement
records.doc: Lean formalization of Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 for every characteristic-zero field and every Weyl-algebra rank, proving that each nonzero d admits F, R, and S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S. The development also proves an exact Bernstein-degree fixed-source strengthening and derived localization, adjoint, and evolutionary results.

records.name: PalomarEGZ.theorem_1_2
records.entry_name: Convex geometry and the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv problem: Theorem 1.2
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1.2 of Dmitrii Zakharov's Convex geometry and the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv problem. For every fixed positive dimension d, as p tends to infinity through the primes, the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant s(F_p^d) satisfies s(F_p^d) = p w(F_p^d) + o(p), where w is the weak Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant.  Supporting proofs include the convex-flag Helly and centerpoint theorems, flag decomposition lemma, balanced convex combinations, relative set expansion, and the polynomial method bound for w. This submission covers Theorem 1.2 and its upper-bound formulation, not every result in the paper. The submission was prepared with the assistance of ChatGPT 5.6 / 6 Sol-Ultra under the direction and review of the author.  The GitHub page includes a PDF file zakharov_2026-3.pdf containing a revised version of the published paper generated  by ChatGPT 5.6 during this formalization project.  The only noteworthy difference is a correction to Definition 4.6 (Proper points) which was meant to use the function f^circ(q) in  place of \hat f(q) in the published version (this typo slipped in during one of the revision rounds of the paper). No other significant mistakes or corrections were discovered.

records.name: Nikodym.card_compl_pow_mul_card_le
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the sharp power saving in the finite-field Nikodym problem. A set N in F_q^d is a Nikodym set if through every point x there is a line all of whose points other than x lie in N. Lower bound: for every finite field F_q, every d >= 2 and every Nikodym set N in F_q^d, |N| >= q^d - (8 d^2 + 1) q^(d - 2^(1-d)); the proof goes through a carrier theorem for integral projective varieties containing many affine lines with private points, proved by finite-grid Hermite interpolation, Hilbert-function estimates (normalized monotonicity and a degree upper bound via linear Noether normalization), an interpolation cut, and a dimension induction that halves the saving at each step. Upper bound: for every d >= 2 and epsilon > 0 and all sufficiently large primes q there is a Nikodym set N in F_q^d with |N| <= q^d - q^(d - 2^(1-d) - epsilon), constructed as the complement of a product set built from a totally real multiquadratic order in which q splits completely, with a digit encoding and tangent lines. Together these give Nik(d, q) = q^d - q^(d - 2^(1-d) + o(1)) along primes. Previously, for general q and d >= 3, the best lower bound was q^d / 2^(d-1) + O(q^(d-1)) and even Nik(d,q) = (1 - o(1)) q^d was open (Lund-Saraf-Wolf, Conjecture 2), while the best upper bounds for prime q were q^d - Omega_d(q^(d - eps_d)) with eps_d << 1/log log d and q^3 - Omega(q^2.1167) (Hunter-Pohoata-Verstraete-Zhang 2026); the lower bound here settles the former conjecture for every finite field, and the construction shows that the exponent d - 1/d conjectured by Chao and Yu (2026) is not sharp over prime fields. The README gives theorem-level comparisons and references. All three headline theorems are proved with no sorry and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: Spherical.eLpNorm_sphericalMaximal_le
records.entry_name: Spherical maximal functions: theorems of Stein and Bourgain
records.doc: This is a Lean 4 formalization of Stein's spherical maximal theorem and Bourgain's circular maximal theorem. The result concerns the sharp range of Lp boundedness of spherical maximal functions in Euclidean space and was first proved by Stein in dimensions three and greater. The much more subtle two-dimensional theorem was first proved by Bourgain. The proof of Bourgain's theorem in this formalization is via Mockenhaupt-Seeger-Sogge's classical argument via a local smoothing estimate for the wave equation. This required first  formalizing various underlying standard results from harmonic analysis. The final theorem statements were written by hand,  while the proofs were almost entirely machine-generated by coding agents with human supervision.

records.name: ContractedBianchi.contractedSecondBianchi
records.entry_name: Double-contracted second Bianchi identity for metric-compatible torsion-free connections
records.doc: Proves the orthonormal double contraction of the actual corrected curvature derivative of a tangent connection on a smooth finite-dimensional real manifold. The Challenge exposes the corrected commutator and the smooth tangent-vector extensions explicitly; the Solution proves the identity for every supplied extension satisfying the stated hypotheses. The derivative symmetries and cyclic Bianchi equations are derived from torsion-freeness and metric compatibility, not assumed as abstract tensor data. No separate Einstein-divergence theorem is selected.

records.name: Combinatorics.Line.exists_of_density_atTop
records.entry_name: The density Hales–Jewett theorem and Szemerédi's theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the density Hales–Jewett theorem: for every finite alphabet α and every density δ > 0, all sufficiently large n have the property that any set of at least δ·|α|^n words of length n over α contains a combinatorial line. The basis for the formalization is the combinatorial proof of Dodos, Kanellopoulos, and Tyros. As a consequence, we also formalize Szemerédi's theorem on the integers: for every k ≥ 3 and δ > 0, the following holds for all sufficiently large n. Any subset of {0, …, n−1} of size at least δ·n contains a nonconstant arithmetic progression of length k.

records.name: Marton.pfr_conjecture
records.doc: A Lean formalization of Marton's conjecture, widely known as the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture, together with its principal consequences. If A is a non-empty subset of an abelian group of exponent 2 with |A + A| <= K|A|, then A is covered by fewer than 2K^12 cosets of a subgroup of cardinality at most |A|; the same conclusion holds with 2K^9 cosets. For an abelian group in which mx = 0 for every x, with m >= 2, the covering number is m * K^(256m^3 + 1). Three consequences are also recorded: a finite set of small doubling in Z^D has a subset of at least K^(-34) of its size whose affine dimension is at most (80/log 2) log K; a map between finite groups of exponent 2 whose additive defects f(x+y) - f(x) - f(y) all lie in a set S differs from a homomorphism by a map taking at most |S|^10 values; and a map that is additive on at least a proportion 1/K of pairs agrees with a homomorphism on at least (|G| / (2^144 K^122) - 1)/2 points. The proofs are by an entropy method: one minimizes a functional of the entropic Ruzsa distance between two random variables and shows the minimum is attained at a uniform distribution on a subgroup, so the development also builds a substantial theory of Shannon entropy, entropic Ruzsa distance, and, for the bounded torsion case, a multidistance for m-tuples. The repository is a collaborative formalization project begun in November 2023; the mathematics is due to the cited papers and nothing here is claimed to be new. The compared theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and on nothing else, and there is no sorry outside the six deliberate holes in PFRPalomar/Challenge.lean.

records.name: Problem56.main_universal_ose
records.entry_name: Subspace embeddings with the rerandomized SRHT
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of a rerandomized SRHT subspace embedding theorem. For every ambient Walsh dimension n = 2^m, rank 1 <= r <= n, and 0 < epsilon < 1, one deterministic width k <= min(n, ceil(C r / epsilon^2)) can be chosen independently of the orthonormal frame. For each fixed frame, the transform with two independent uniform sign layers and an independent uniform k-subset has spectral failure probability at most 1/100, and preserves all squared norms in that subspace within 1 +/- epsilon with probability at least 99/100. C is an explicit universal constant, with no sharp numerical value claimed. The Comparator selects the spectral theorem and its fixed-frame squared-norm consequence. The full repository retains the 12 named v6 results and their supporting proofs and correspondence maps.

For each fixed frame, the transform with two independent uniform sign layers and an independent uniform k-subset has spectral failure probability at most 1/100, and preserves all squared norms in that subspace within 1 +/- epsilon with probability at least 99/100. C is an explicit universal constant, with no sharp numerical value claimed. The Comparator selects the spectral theorem and its fixed-frame squared-norm consequence. The full repository retains the 12 named v6 results and their supporting proofs and correspondence maps.

records.name: BN.lambda1_sq_add_lambda2_sq_le
records.entry_name: A proof of the Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture in Lean
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture (2007) and of the matrix theorems that prove it. Let G be a finite simple graph with adjacency eigenvalues lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= ..., m edges and clique number omega(G). The conjecture states that every noncomplete graph on at least two vertices satisfies lambda_1^2 + lambda_2^2 <= 2 (1 - 1/omega(G)) m. The formalization proves it (BN.lambda1_sq_add_lambda2_sq_le) as a consequence of a weighted spectral inequality: for every symmetric entrywise nonnegative matrix B with zero diagonal supported on the edges of G, the sum F(B) of the squares of the two largest positive eigenvalues of B is at most (1 - 1/omega(G)) ||B||_F^2 (BN.weighted). The weighted inequality rests on a complete-positivity theorem for planar Gram matrices: if z_1, ..., z_n in R^2 lie in a closed half-plane through the origin and X is their Gram matrix, then M(X) = X o X + sum over i < j with X_ij < 0 of X_ij^2 (e_i - e_j)(e_i - e_j)^T is completely positive (BN.matrix_theorem), proved by an ordered elimination, a Schur complement identified as a weighted Laplacian plus a matrix with an explicit three-column nonnegative factorization, and total nonnegativity of two rectangular kernels. A variational argument then removes the half-plane hypothesis from the scalar inequality: for every real positive semidefinite X of rank at most two, sum_{i,j} (A_G)_ij (X_ij)_+^2 <= (1 - 1/omega(G)) ||X||_F^2 (BN.gram_le), which also identifies the rank-two conic parameter chi''_{vec,3}(G) of Coutinho, Spier and Zhang with omega(G) (BN.chiVec3_eq_cliqueNum), settling their Conjectures 2 and 3 without a lower bound on the clique number. Previously the conjecture was known for weakly perfect graphs (Ando–Lin), triangle-free graphs (Lin–Ning–Wu), regular graphs (Zhang), graphs with few triangles (Kumar–Pragada, Zeng–Zhang), asymptotically almost surely for random graphs (Liu–Bu), and with weaker constants for all graphs (Coutinho–Spier–Zhang). All five headline theorems are proved with no sorry and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: ShellTomography.Verified.trade_criterion
records.entry_name: Distance-shell tomography: product kernels and sharp grid sensing
records.doc: General integer-trade criterion and full-factor Cartesian-product kernel/recovery theorem; the all-order grid lower bound; and, for every n ≥ 6, the complete four-parameter integer grid kernel, exact threshold n−2 for odd n and n−3 for even n, optimal n−2 sensor count throughout 2 ≤ h < threshold, and unique four-parameter description of equal-observation populations.

records.name: PalomarRR.nonM_minimum
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the lower bound non(M) ≤ rr, where non(M) is the least cardinality of a nonmeagre subset of the usual real line and rr is the least cardinality of a family of permutations of the natural numbers that changes the sum or destroys convergence of every conditionally convergent real series. It accompanies the manuscript *Determining the Rearrangement Number* by Vinicius de Oliveira Rodrigues. The reverse inequality was already known in the literature. The reverse inequality, the full equality, and further manuscript corollaries are not formalized in this project.

records.name: PalomarHlawkaSchatten.dimension_independent_hlawka_constant_for_schatten_norms
records.entry_name: Dimension-independent Hlawka constants for Schatten norms
records.doc: Existence of a dimension-independent Hlawka constant for every Schatten p-norm with 1 < p < infinity, and proof that no such constant exists at either endpoint (trace norm at p=1, operator norm at p=infinity).
